ideas.title: California Prop 99 three ways: DID, synthetic control and SDID on the real panel, against Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) Table 1 and synthdid
ideas.anchor_notebook: notebooks/29_synthetic_did.py (also notebooks/24_synthetic_control.py; both run on simulated panels today)
ideas.question: Does puremacro reproduce Table 1 of Arkhangelsky et al. on California's Proposition 99, and why do SDID, SC and DID disagree?
ideas.description: Replace the simulated panels in 29 and 24 with the 39-state 1970-2000 per-capita cigarette panel (California treated from 1989). Compute DID, SC and SDID, the unit and time weights, placebo standard errors and the ADH gap plot, then add a sub-second ReplicationCase. Session check (scratch sdid_check*.py, sc_check*.py): synthetic_did returns tau = -27.35 with exactly uniform omega = 1/38 and lambda = 1/19. SLSQP stops with 'Positive directional derivative for linesearch' and _solve_simplex_quadratic silently returns the starting point (puremacro/did/synthetic_did.py:88), so SDID collapses to plain DID (-27.35). Dividing the outcomes by their s.d. lets SLSQP converge and gives tau = -15.19. puremacro/synthetic_control.py (fallback at :154) gives pre-RMSE 22.3 packs and a post gap of -46.1 at raw scale. After rescaling it gives 1.66 and -19.51, with weights Utah .394, Montana .232, Nevada .205, Connecticut .109. puremacro/causal/synthetic_control.py (:36, no success check), which notebook 24 uses, gives a post ATT of -41.7.
ideas.paper: Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens & Wager (2021 AER) 'Synthetic Difference-in-Differences'; Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller (2010 JASA)
ideas.oracle_detail: Read this session in arXiv 1812.09970, p.8, Table 1: SDID -15.6 (8.4), SC -19.6 (9.9), DID -27.3 (17.7), MC -20.2 (11.5), DIFP -11.1 (9.5); placebo-method SEs. Second oracle: R synthdid 0.0.9 (BSD-3). Freeze synthdid_estimate, sc_estimate, did_estimate and vcov(method='placebo') as a fixture. ADH (2010) Table 2 donor weights and predictor balance: to transcribe from ADH JASA 2010 (Synth R output as numbers only).
ideas.data_detail: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/synth-inference/synthdid/master/data/california_prop99.csv (1,209 rows, ';'-separated: State, Year, PacksPerCapita, treated; 32.7 KB). The package DESCRIPTION reads 'GPL (>= 2) | BSD_3_clause' and GitHub reports BSD-3-Clause (both read this session), so it can be bundled in puremacro/replication/data with the Stanford notice. Cite ADH (2010) and the Orzechowski-Walker Tax Burden on Tobacco. Note: examples/synthetic_did_california_prop99.py is simulated despite its name.
ideas.library_gaps: (1) Scale-dependent weight solvers that fail silently: standardise Y internally or use Frank-Wolfe as synthdid does, and warn or raise instead of returning uniform weights (did/synthetic_did.py:88, synthetic_control.py:154-165 fixed-step projected-gradient fallback, causal/synthetic_control.py:36). (2) There is no placebo variance estimator (AAHIW Section 5) for N_tr = 1; the donor bootstrap is used instead. (3) No DIFP or matrix-completion estimators. (4) No ADH predictor V-matrix optimisation. (5) Two divergent SC implementations should be unified.
ideas.plan_overlap: Not in PLAN.md or the 09-20 review. It supersedes the simulated example and fixes the estimators behind notebooks 24 and 29.

vets.required_changes:
1. **Rewrite the diagnosis.** Attribute the -15.19 vs -15.6 gap to the noise-level definition (did/synthetic_did.py:109-111), not to lambda regularisation or solver tolerance. Add a noise_level option ('demeaned' as default, 'synthdid', or a float) so the invariance test at tests/test_did/test_audit_regressions.py:208 still passes. Use 'synthdid' in the replication and state the deliberate deviation in the notebook.
2. **Replace SLSQP in all three solvers** (did/synthetic_did.py:54-91, synthetic_control.py:136-165, causal/synthetic_control.py:29-37) with a scale-robust simplex-ridge QP solver, such as Frank-Wolfe with exact line search as in synthdid solver.R, or scaled active-set. Add an optimality check that warns or raises. A res.success check alone will not catch the false success at the uniform start. Add regression tests on the raw Prop 99 panel and on a x1000-scaled copy.
3. **Fix the causal SC off-by-one** (causal/synthetic_control.py:25), or retire that module and point notebook 24 at a single unified synthetic_control.
4. **Add AAHIW Algorithm 4 placebo variance** (se_method='placebo', mirroring synthdid vcov.R placebo_se).
5. **Keep the ReplicationCase to point estimates.**
   - SDID, SC and DID at TIGHT, which needs the synthdid noise level for SDID; with the default noise level SDID only passes at MEDIUM.
   - DIFP -11.1 optional.
   - Placebo SEs in the notebook only, or COARSE with a fixed seed. My port's 200-rep SEs were 8.42, 10.51 and 16.41 against 8.4, 9.9 and 17.7.
6. **Drop two oracles.** Drop ADH Table 2 donor weights and predictor balance: the synthdid CSV has no covariates and there is no V-matrix step. Use synthdid sc_estimate weights instead (port: Utah .396, Montana .232, Nevada .204, Connecticut .104, New Hampshire .045, Colorado .013). Drop MC or defer it.
7. **Build the synthdid fixture explicitly.** Install synthdid 0.0.9 into the existing rconv R env as a one-off, recording the version or commit. Freeze estimates, weights and placebo SEs. Compare weights loosely, because FW early stopping and sparsify leave SC at -19.62 while the exact optimum is -19.52.
8. **Vendor the data.** Convert the CSV to ',' separators or add a separator argument to replication/_data.py:14. Ship the Stanford BSD-3 notice and cite ADH 2010 and Orzechowski-Walker.
9. **Plan for the full scope** (medium cost, not low):
   - Rebuild notebooks 24, 24_es, 29 and 29_es, with their executed .ipynb files.
   - Fix notebook 29's math cell, which omits the intercepts and ridge scaling and claims "unbiased if either weight balances".
   - Rewrite examples/synthetic_did_california_prop99.py.
   - Update EXAMPLES_CATALOG.md:202, docs/examples_gallery.md:537, notebooks/README.md, docs/notebooks.md and docs/es/notebooks.md.
10. **Correct the merged risk note.** Notebooks 24 and 29 do not hit the fallback at their current simulated scales (0 of 202 failures for notebook 29).
vets.capabilities_check:
Every listed symbol exists at its stated path: synthetic_did at puremacro/did/synthetic_did.py:134, synthetic_control at puremacro/synthetic_control.py:168 (SLSQP at :152, fallback at :154-164), causal synthetic_control at puremacro/causal/synthetic_control.py:9 (no success check at :36-37), and sdid_multi_cohort at puremacro/did/sdid_multi.py:170, which wraps synthetic_did at :158 and so inherits the bug.

I reproduced the core claim on the real panel (work env, scipy 1.18.1). synthetic_did gives tau = -27.349 with omega exactly 1/38 and lambda exactly 1/19. Both SLSQP calls fail with 'Positive directional derivative for linesearch' (omega after 62 iterations, lambda after 12), and synthetic_did.py:88-89 silently returns the start point.

The SC numbers did NOT reproduce as stated, and the real failure is worse than the proposal says:
- **puremacro/synthetic_control.py:** SLSQP reports success=True after 5 iterations and returns exactly the uniform start. That gives pre-RMSE 16.04 and a gap of -41.71 in both the work env (numpy 2.4.6) and .venv (numpy 2.5.2). The fallback path at :154 is what yields RMSE 22.31. A res.success check therefore cannot catch this.
- **causal/synthetic_control.py:** the raw-scale result depends on the numpy version: -19.70 in the work env versus -41.71 (uniform weights) in .venv. It also has an off-by-one at :25 (T_pre = treat_time - 1 drops 1988 from the fit).
- **After rescaling,** synthetic_control gives RMSE 1.66, gap -19.51, and weights Utah .394, Montana .232, Nevada .205, Connecticut .109, New Hampshire .045, Colorado .015. This matches the proposal.
- **Today's notebooks are unaffected:** notebook 29's simulated panel has 0 of 202 SLSQP failures. The same panel multiplied by 10 fails 1 of 2 calls.

Missing pieces: there is no placebo SE; the donor-only bootstrap at synthetic_did.py:254-273 is a variant for which synthdid returns NA when N_tr = 1. There is also no noise-level option and no DIFP or MC estimator.
vets.oracle_check:
I verified Table 1 this session from arXiv 1812.09970 (PDF downloaded, page 8 text extracted with pypdf): SDID -15.6 (8.4), SC -19.6 (9.9), DID -27.3 (17.7), MC -20.2 (11.5), DIFP -11.1 (9.5), with placebo-method SEs over 12 post years.

I ported synthdid 0.0.9's Frank-Wolfe solver to Python from solver.R and synthdid.R, fetched from GitHub master (scratch fwport.py). The port reproduces SDID -15.604, SC -19.620, DID -27.349, and DIFP -11.105 (SC with intercept, uniform lambda, eta 1e-6). Its placebo SEs over 200 reps are 8.42, 10.51 and 16.41, so the SEs match only within Monte Carlo noise.

Solving the weight problems exactly (not via synthdid's early-stopped FW):
- **SDID** is -15.606 with synthdid's noise level and -15.192 with puremacro's period-demeaned noise level.
- **SC** is -19.518. The published -19.6 is a product of synthdid's early FW stopping plus its sparsify pass.

The R fixture is obtainable but not ready. R exists in the conda env rconv, but synthdid is not installed there, and the synthdid README prints no outputs. The ADH (2010) Table 2 oracle is unreachable from this dataset (see data_check).

vets.oracle_check:
The oracle is real, independent and obtainable. I fetched arXiv 1812.09970 in this session and read p.8 with pypdf. Table 1 reads: SDID -15.6 (8.4), SC -19.6 (9.9), DID -27.3 (17.7), MC -20.2 (11.5), DIFP -11.1 (9.5), all with 'placebo method' SEs.

I also fetched the synthdid 0.0.9 source this session (R/synthdid.R, solver.R, vcov.R, utils.R). A roughly 60-line numpy port of its Frank-Wolfe code with sparsify reproduces the table:
- SDID -15.604, SC -19.620, DID -27.349.
- DIFP -11.105, defined as omega with intercept, eta 1e-6 and uniform lambda.
- Without the sparsify step: SDID -15.611 and SC -19.587. The sparsify step is immaterial.

The proposal's explanation of the remaining gap is WRONG. The -15.19 vs -15.6 difference is not lambda regularisation or solver tolerance. It comes from the period-demeaned noise level at did/synthetic_did.py:109-111 (sigma 4.448 vs synthdid's sd of raw first differences, 5.494). The port with the demeaned sigma gives -15.184.

Standard errors: synthdid's placebo SE is Monte Carlo, with 200 draws taken with replacement from only 38 placebos.
- Exact enumeration over all 38 placebos gives SDID 9.37, SC 10.62, DID 17.29.
- The R-style 200-replicate 5-95% bands are SDID [8.29, 10.41], SC [9.13, 11.95], DID [14.86, 19.45].
- The published SEs fall inside these bands. SDID's 8.4 sits near the band's lower edge.
- So SEs can only be band-checked, never matched to one decimal.

R is not installed here (no R, Rscript, rpy2 or cvxpy), so the frozen synthdid fixture needs an R install. It is optional given Table 1.

ADH Table 2 (read in NBER w12831 p.49): Utah .334, Nevada .234, Montana .199, Colorado .164, Connecticut .069. These weights cannot be a pass/fail target:
- The synthdid CSV has no predictors.
- puremacro has no V-matrix optimisation.
- Outcome-only SC gives Utah .396, Montana .232, Nevada .204, Connecticut .104, New Hampshire .045, Colorado .013.

Data vintage check: California's 1975/1980/1988 values in the CSV (127.1/120.2/90.1) match ADH Table 1 (w12831 p.48).

ideas.title: High-frequency monetary shocks on real data: Gertler-Karadi (2015) proxy SVAR and Jarocinski-Karadi (2020) information effects
ideas.question: Do FOMC-window futures surprises identify a monetary shock that moves the 1-year rate, output, prices and credit spreads as GK report, and how strong is the instrument?
ideas.description: Replace puremacro/examples/hfi_gertler_karadi.py. Its instrument is simulated independently of the VAR (lines 31, 36, 41), so OP F = 3.27 and the plotted 'MP shock' IRFs identify nothing. Build the GK instrument from their surprise series, estimate the 4-variable (and EBP) proxy SVAR, report the first-stage F with robust bands, and add Jarocinski-Karadi poor-man sign splitting as an exercise.
ideas.paper: Gertler and Karadi (2015) AEJ:Macro 7(1); Jarocinski and Karadi (2020) AEJ:Macro
ideas.oracle_detail: GK (2015, AEJ:Macro): the first-stage F and IRFs for the 1-year rate, IP, CPI and EBP. To be read from the paper's table and figures (not read this session); exact re-estimation is possible from the replication files.
ideas.data_detail: openICPSR project 114082 (GK 2015 replication data; may require a free login). Jarocinski-Karadi shocks are public on GitHub. Freeze monthly series with a provenance card.
ideas.library_gaps: puremacro/hfi has constructors (gk2015_surprise, ns2018_first_pc, jk_poor_man) but no real-data loader. Check that proxy_svar handles an instrument sample shorter than the VAR sample (GK: VAR 1979-2012, instrument 1991-2012), and that weak-IV-robust bands exist for proxy SVAR rather than only for LP-IV.
ideas.plan_overlap: Not in PLAN.md. Serves the 09-20 'instrument strength vs validity' lab.

vets.required_changes:
1. Scope: one bilingual notebook plus replacement of puremacro/examples/hfi_gertler_karadi.py. Drop the NS-2018 and LP-IV sections, or make them exercises.
2. Instrument: FF4 30-min surprises from the JK CC-BY file (1991:01-2012:06), aggregated with a new GK 31-day monthly-average helper. Show the calendar-sum contrast (robust F about 8 against 17) as the instrument-strength lesson.
3. VAR: GS1, 100*log IP, 100*log CPI, EBP for 1979:07-2012:06 with p=12. Report plain F, OP F on the subsample, bootstrap bands, and the impact-ratio AR band from msw_bands, clearly labelled as impact-only. Do not claim full MSW IRF bands unless MSW-2021 is implemented.
4. Extend proxy_svar to accept a shorter or NaN-masked instrument sample, so the reported first_stage_F is the 1991-2012 statistic (17.29), not the zero-padded one (16.61).
5. Replace jk_median_target with a port of JK's signrestr_median.m and add golden tests against published MP_median/CBI_median (tolerance 1e-7) and MP_pm/CBI_pm.
6. Oracle: use NBER WP w20224 values with tolerance bands (robust F in about [15, 20], R2 about 0.075-0.08, N = 258, GS1 impact about 0.2-0.3), plus the JK published shock series for exact checks. Mark the AEJ published table as unverified until someone reads it.
7. Freeze gk15_monthly.csv and jk_fomc_surprises.csv via a tools/gen_notebook_data_hfi.py script into puremacro/replication/data, with a provenance card: JK CC BY 4.0 attribution, FRED IDs, EBP vintage date.
8. Optional: fix gk2015_surprise (m/(m-d) convention and FF2 switch) and the ns2018_first_pc scaling. Correct the proposal's event count (330 events in the update, not 325).
vets.capabilities_check:
All five symbols exist, but two of them do not do what the proposal needs. Smoke scripts are in scratchpad/wf/hfi-gk-review/ (smoke_jk.py, smoke_gk.py).
(1) jk_poor_man (puremacro/hfi/jk2020.py:23-66) is correct. On the authors' 330-event file it reproduces the published MP_pm/CBI_pm exactly (max|diff| = 0).
(2) jk_median_target (jk2020.py:74-147) is wrong. The admissible test at :130 does not depend on the data, so the median angle at :137 is always -46.56 deg; I got the same angle on pure noise. :140 rotates the raw (pc1, SP500) pair, which mixes units. MP+CBI does not add up to pc1 (max gap 0.26). Against the published MP_median/CBI_median: corr 0.92 / 0.57, max|diff| 3.04. A 25-line port of JK's signrestr_median.m (QR-based, BSD-3) matches the published series to 5e-9. tests/test_hfi/test_jk2020.py:45-58 only checks orthogonality and the method label.
(3) aggregate_to_period (surprises.py:123-153) works as a calendar-month sum and matches JK's monthly pc1 (434 months, diff 3e-17). It is NOT GK's aggregation: GK cumulate over the last 31 days and average across the days of the month.
(4) gk2015_surprise (surprises.py:14-59) is not needed, because the GK baseline FF4 takes no day-count scaling. Its docstring (:33-35) defines days remaining as including the announcement day, which gives m/(m-d+1). The GSS MP1 in the JK file equals FF1*m/(m-d) in 57 of 57 events, so it is off by one day. It has no FF2 switch for meetings in the last week of the month.
(5) proxy_svar (puremacro/var/identify/proxy.py:74-170) works on real data. It takes the last T_eff values of the instrument (:134) and has no way to use an instrument sample shorter than the VAR sample. A NaN-padded instrument raises LinAlgError 'SVD did not converge'. With zero padding the direction is fine, but first_stage_F (:136) is computed over the whole padded 1979-2012 sample: 16.61, against 17.29 on the correct 1991:01-2012:06 subsample.
(6) msw_bands (puremacro/inference/weak_iv.py:418-450) is scalar Anderson-Rubin grid inversion, not the Montiel Olea-Stock-Watson (2021) SVAR-IV confidence sets. It works for the impact ratio only: EBP/GS1 impact 0.614, 95% AR band [0.110, 1.460]. There is nothing for IRFs at h>0.
(7) ns2018_first_pc correlates 0.9995 with JK's pc1, but the scale differs (std ratio 0.878). JK standardise the contracts, run an uncentred PCA, zero-fill missing values and scale to the std of ED4.
The existing puremacro/examples/hfi_gertler_karadi.py is confirmed broken. Lines 31/36/41 draw the macro data and the surprise independently. OP F = 3.2745 is also computed on the IP_growth residual (default shock_target_idx=0 at :44, while the FFR is column 2); on the FFR residual F = 0.0002.
vets.oracle_check:
The published AEJ PDF (pubs.aeaweb.org) and openICPSR both return 403. I read the numbers this session from NBER WP w20224 (2014, nber.org; pypdf text of Table 3 and the Figure 1 note):
- VAR sample 1979:07-2012:06; instrument sample 1991:01-2012:06.
- Monthly surprise = cumulate over the last 31 days, then average across the days of the month (footnote 11).
- Table 3, column (2), FF4 on the 1-year-rate residual: R2 0.078, robust F 17.50, N 258.
- Figure 1 note: F 21.55, robust F 17.64, R2 7.76%.
- Text: a one-standard-deviation shock raises the 1-year rate by 'roughly twenty five basis point'.
The lag length is not stated in the WP. My public-data rebuild with p=12 (JK FF4 + current FRED GS1/INDPRO + bundled CPIAUCSL + Fed EBP) gives subsample F 21.81, OP/robust F 17.29, R2 0.0785, N 258, and a 1-s.d. impact on GS1 of +0.239. So the oracle is reachable, within about 2% on public data. With a calendar-month sum instead of GK's averaging, robust F falls to 8.33 (R2 0.048), which shows the aggregation choice decides whether the instrument looks strong.
For JK, the published shock series are a stronger oracle: poor-man is exact, and median-target is exact after porting signrestr_median.m. Treat the AEJ published values as a pending cross-check unless someone with access confirms them.

ideas.title: Arellano-Bond (1991) employment equations: difference and system GMM against the Stata xtabond manual
ideas.question: Does ab_gmm reproduce AB (1991) Table 4 col a1 on the canonical UK firm panel, and what do Nickell bias, instrument proliferation (collapse), Windmeijer correction and Blundell-Bond system GMM change?
ideas.description: Load abdata: 140 firms, 1976-1984, unbalanced. Estimate the xtabond specification: n on L(1/2).n, L(0/1).w, L(0/2).(k ys), year dummies and a trend. Run one-step, then two-step with Windmeijer SEs. Show the AR(1)/AR(2) tests and Hansen J, collapsed versus uncollapsed instruments, and bb_gmm. Add a Monte Carlo that shows Nickell bias of within-FE and the weak-instrument collapse of difference GMM as rho approaches 1 (simulation truth, reusing the dynpanel validation DGP). Probe this session: ab_gmm and bb_gmm with collapse=False raise LinAlgError 'Z'HZ not positive definite' on abdata even for the pure AR(2) (28x28), so the paper's uncollapsed estimator cannot run on the canonical unbalanced panel. With collapse=True and X_pred=[w,k,ys], ab_gmm gives L1.n=0.559 and L2.n=-0.088.
ideas.oracle_detail: Stata xtabond manual (stata.com/manuals/xtxtabond.pdf, read this session). One-step homoskedastic: L1.n .6862261, L2.n -.0853582, 'identical to those reported in column a1 of table 4'. Two-step WC-robust: L1.n .6287089 (se .1934138), L2.n -.0651882 (se .0450501). 611 obs, 140 groups, 41 instruments. linearmodels 7.0 is installed locally as a second route.
ideas.data_detail: https://www.stata-press.com/data/r17/abdata.dta (108 KB, pandas.read_stata reads it; has n, w, k, ys, yr1976-yr1984) or Rdatasets plm/EmplUK.csv (50 KB, raw levels, log them). Both fetched OK this session.
ideas.library_gaps: (1) The uncollapsed instrument matrix is singular on unbalanced panels (the weight inversion at ab_gmm.py:75 uses a Cholesky _inv_psd). Stata and xtabond2 use a generalized inverse or drop empty instrument columns. (2) tests/test_dynpanel/test_ab_1991_replication.py:37-54 asserts L1.n=0.474, L2.n=-0.053 as 'Table 4 col 2' using collapse=True with X_pred. Those targets do not match the Stata-reported col a1 or two-step values, and this session's run of that exact call on abdata gives 0.559, so the test would fail if tests/fixtures/abdata.csv existed. It is absent, so the test always skips and has never run.
ideas.plan_overlap: None. The dynpanel validation cases (puremacro/validation/cases_dynpanel.py) use DGP references only.

vets.capabilities_check:
All five symbols exist at the stated paths: ab_gmm (ab_gmm.py:125), bb_gmm (bb_gmm.py:246), ar_test (diagnostics.py:62), hansen_j (diagnostics.py:33) and windmeijer_correction (diagnostics.py:148). I ran the exact xtabond spec on abdata (scratch wf/adv-ab91/repro.py, wc.py, ar_bb.py). The strictly exogenous regressors were passed as X_exog with lags built by groupby-shift: [w, L1w, k, L1k, L2k, ys, L1ys, L2ys, yr1980-84, year]; year stands in for noconstant+trend. Findings:
(1) As shipped, collapse=False raises LinAlgError at ab_gmm.py:75. The cause is exactly one all-zero instrument column, '_yL0_L2@t1978'. The uncollapsed basis (instruments.py:292-300) is built from diff times before rows lacking lag 2 are dropped (instruments.py:591-596). After monkeypatching that column away, Z is 611x41, the same as Stata's 41 instruments and 611 obs.
(2) With that patch, one-step coefficients match Stata to within 5e-8. One-step cluster-robust SEs match Example 2 to 7 decimals (L1.n SE .1445943, L2.n SE .0560155, which are AB col a1). Two-step coefficients match Example 4 to within 5e-8 (L1.n .6287089).
(3) The Windmeijer SEs are wrong. They come out 1.01x to 1.68x Stata's WC-robust values: L1.n .2275 vs .1934138, L2.n .0580 vs .0450501, w .2602 vs .1546107. The bug is at diagnostics.py:234, where dS/dbeta uses step-2 residuals. Evaluating it at the step-1 residuals, as Windmeijer (2005) does, reproduces all 16 Stata SEs (ratio 1.00000). windmeijer=True is the default in both ab_gmm and bb_gmm.
(4) ar_test is the residual-only variant. It gives AR(1) z=-4.147 and AR(2) z=-0.449 against Stata's -3.5996 and -.51603. The full AB m_j formula (about 25 lines, using the Z/X_diff/W kwargs already in the signature at diagnostics.py:67-69) reproduces -3.59959 and -0.51603. GMMResult stores only p-values, not z.
(5) One-step output is robust-only (ab_gmm.py:222-244), and the one-step 'J' is evaluated at W2 (ab_gmm.py:298-301). Homoskedastic SE and Sargan are missing, but sigma2=u'u/(2(n-k)) reproduces Stata's .1486163/.0444365 and Sargan 65.81806 (read this session).
(6) bb_gmm cannot serve as the system-GMM leg:
- On the xtdpdsys manual spec (n L(0/2).(w k) yr1980-yr1984 year) it raises LinAlgError for both collapse settings.
- On the X_pred spec it gives L1.n=0.359, below AB's 0.559. That is the opposite of xtdpdsys (.8221535 vs .6286618, read this session) and of the Blundell-Bond story.
- Structural causes: the level block is always collapsed (bb_gmm.py:127-139); there is no level constant, and a ones column makes Z_diff singular; exog levels are used as level instruments (bb_gmm.py:186-190); the step-1 weight is Z'Z (bb_gmm.py:229); and n_obs counts stacked rows (bb_gmm.py:470).
The test-spec claim holds: collapse=True with X_pred gives L1.n=0.5589 and L2.n=-0.0881. The Monte Carlo works with dynpanel_demo_data (about 60 ms per replication at N=200, T=7). At rho=0.9 the means are FE 0.51, AB 0.63 (sd 0.44) and BB 0.88. At rho=0.98 they are FE 0.57, AB 0.03 (sd 0.54) and BB 0.93.

(5) bb_gmm fails on the xtdpdsys spec in all four collapse/two_step combinations: Z'Z is singular when uncollapsed, and the step-2 weight is singular when collapsed. Even in one-step mode it builds W2 for J (bb_gmm.py:180). It also has no level constant. It uses X_exog levels as level instruments and always collapses the LD.n level block (bb_gmm.py:127-137, 186-191). Its step-1 weight is Z'Z (bb_gmm.py:229-238), and the endogenous level instrument is Delta x_t, not Delta x_{t-1} (bb_gmm.py:172-178). A hand-built system with blockdiag(H_d, I), 7 uncollapsed LD.n columns and _cons gives 47 instruments and L1.n 0.8221535, which exactly matches xtdpdsys.

(6) The xtabond predetermined examples cannot be expressed in ab_gmm. Stata Examples 6 and 8 need L.w as a regressor instrumented by lags of w, and ab_gmm ties every regressor to its own lag block (instruments.py:341-355). Scope should stay with Examples 1-4 (strictly exogenous regressors).

(7) The Monte Carlo is feasible and fast: 4 rho values x 50 reps of within-FE, ab_gmm and bb_gmm take 5.6 s on the dynpanel_demo_data DGP (cases_dynpanel.py). It shows Nickell bias (FE mean 0.07 at rho=.3, 0.51 at rho=.9) and difference-GMM collapse (AB mean 0.47, sd 0.46 at rho=.9; mean 0.33, sd 0.58 at rho=.95), against BB means of 0.87 and 0.79.

ideas.title: Shift-share IV done right: AKM placebo coverage, BHJ shock-level equivalence and GPSS Rotemberg weights, applied to the ADH (2013) China shock
ideas.question: How much wider is inference on the China-shock effect on manufacturing employment when regions exposed to the same sectors are treated as correlated (AKM) rather than independent (EHW), and which industries drive the Bartik instrument?
ideas.description: Estimate the ADH commuting-zone IV of the change in manufacturing employment share on import exposure, instrumented by other-country exposure through industry shares. Report EHW and AKM SEs from shift_share_iv, first-stage strength (olea_pflueger_f, kleibergen_paap_f, stock_yogo_cv) and weak-IV-robust AR sets (anderson_rubin_test, msw_bands). Show the Rotemberg weights (Goldsmith-Pinkham, Sorkin and Swift 2020) and the top-5 industries. Add a placebo Monte Carlo that draws random sector shocks: EHW over-rejects while AKM holds size (the design of tests/test_spatial/test_shift_share_iv.py:40, on real shares).
ideas.oracle_detail: ShiftShareSE CRAN vignette (read this session). IV estimate -0.7742267 with EHW SE 0.1647892, AKM SE 0.2403730 and AKM0 CI (-1.6903240, -0.3893132). Reduced form -0.4885687 (EHW 0.1124436, AKM 0.16419445). First stage 0.6310409 (EHW 0.08700719, AKM 0.05296055).
ideas.data_detail: github.com/kolesarm/ShiftShareSE/master/data/ADH.rda (1.19 MB: regional data, share matrix W and sector shocks; HEAD 200). It is in R format, so it needs a one-time offline conversion to CSV/NPZ for a Pyodide fixture. The ADH file archive at ddorn.net (2.95 MB zip of .dta) is a second source.
ideas.library_gaps: shift_share_iv supports se in {'akm','robust'} only (akm.py:181), so the AKM0 (null-imposed, weak-IV-valid) interval is missing. No handling of collinear sector shares (see the vignette discussion). The other bartik builders (build_county_epu, estimate_industry_sensitivities, build_exposure_iv) are specific to the county-EPU/QCEW project and are not a general API. The whole bartik package has 0 notebook and 0 example call sites.
ideas.plan_overlap: None in PLAN.md. The weak-IV pieces overlap notebook 28 (lp_iv AR) and the planned notebook-35 rebuild (Ramey-Zubairy AR/MSW).

ideas.title: Staggered DiD in practice: honest bounds on Medicaid expansion, pre-trend power and the CS/SA/BJS/dCDH/SDID zoo
ideas.question: How large a violation of parallel trends can the ACA Medicaid-expansion effect on insurance coverage survive, and do CS, SA, BJS, CdH and multi-cohort SDID agree once all adoption cohorts are used?
ideas.description: Step 1 is a non-staggered TWFE event study (2014 adopters against never-treated, years before 2016) with regress.ols clustered by state, then honest_did with smoothness (FLCI) and relative magnitudes, with the sensitivity plot and breakdown M. It teaches that small-sample corrections with absorbed FE move the CIs. Step 2 uses all cohorts (2014-2019) with callaway_santanna, sun_abraham, borusyak_jaravel_spiess, cdh_did and sdid_multi_cohort, then honest_did on the CS event study. Probe this session: with fixest-style degrees of freedom (K=7 non-absorbed regressors), puremacro's SD FLCIs are M=0 [0.0262,0.0605], M=0.01 [0.0135,0.0785] and M=0.05 [-0.0269,0.1205]. The published values are [0.0259,0.0607], [0.0132,0.0787] and [-0.0271,0.121]. Counting FE in the degrees of freedom widens puremacro's CIs by about 7%. The staggered run works: BJS ATT(0)=0.051, CdH DID_M=0.045, SDID-multi ATT=0.070.

ideas.library_gaps: The relative-magnitudes CI uses Imbens-Manski, not RR's conditional/hybrid (C-LF). This is documented at did/sensitivity.py:58 and :1063 and gives about 1e-3 differences against the README. ideas.title: Uncertainty and coverage lab for staggered DiD: pointwise, sup-t and overall-ATT intervals with shared controls
ideas.question: How often do pointwise, simultaneous and overall-ATT intervals contain a planted treatment effect, and how do shared controls and cluster counts change that?
ideas.description: Status: not implemented. 10 reports one seeded miss ([1.020, 1.252] around 1.129 against truth 1.0, per the 09-20 REVIEW). DGP: notebook 10's two-way fixed-effects panel (T=14, cohorts 5/8/11 plus never-treated, sigma=0.3). Cells: constant ATT=1 or dynamic 0.5+0.1e; never-treated share 25% or 8% (shared-control dependence); N in {60,180}; and an arm with a linear pre-trend violation. Each replication runs callaway_santanna(n_boot=100) and sun_abraham(n_boot=100) (about 90 ms together natively, about 145 ms in Pyodide) and records pointwise coverage by event time, simultaneous coverage over e=0..5, and the MC s.d. of the SA estimate against its reported se. On R=100 only, it also runs the overall-ATT whole-unit bootstrap (B=99 calls to callaway_santanna(n_boot=0): 0.2 s native, 0.33 s Pyodide per replication). honest_did(result=cs) runs on pre-trend draws (127 ms per call). Prototype (R=100, 25% never-treated): pointwise 90% coverage for e=0..5 was 0.85-0.97 (SA) and 0.80-0.93 (CS); simultaneous coverage was 0.63-0.66 (SA) and 0.48-0.55 (CS). Budget about 60-90 s in Pyodide at R=200 per cell for the main grid; use runtime.fit and longrun.chunked. Figure: (a) coverage by event time with ±2 MC s.e. against nominal 90%; (b) simultaneous vs pointwise coverage by never-treated share; (c) ratio of reported SA se to MC s.d. by e. Exercise: change the never-treated share or N. Assert that the MC mean ATT is within 3 MC s.e. of the truth and that simultaneous coverage <= the minimum pointwise coverage (an identity).
ideas.paper: Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021); Sun and Abraham (2021); Borusyak, Jaravel and Spiess (2024); Rambachan and Roth (2023); Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Moller (2019)
ideas.oracle_detail: The ATT path is planted. Coverage is a frequency with MC s.e. sqrt(p(1-p)/R); the SA se check compares the reported se with the Monte Carlo s.d. of the same estimator.
ideas.data_detail: Simulated balanced panels (notebook 10 DGP generator, vectorised).
ideas.library_gaps: (1) att_overall has no standard error or interval in CallawaySantannaResult (callaway_santanna.py:253), SunAbrahamResult (sun_abraham.py:139-144) or the BJS result, so every overall interval needs a nested unit bootstrap, the main Monte Carlo cost. (2) The SA event-study se is sqrt(sum w^2 se^2) (sun_abraham.py:121-127) and omits cross-cohort covariance from shared controls (09-20 REVIEW finding 2); the lab measures the consequence. (3) The CS bootstrap draws are not exposed, so supt_band(draws=...) cannot build simultaneous bands; suggestion: return the draws or add overall_ci=True.
ideas.plan_overlap: 09-20 REVIEW brainstorm item 2 and finding 2 (Sun-Abraham audit). Not in PLAN.md. honest_did and supt_band have no notebook use apart from a mention in 00.

vets.required_changes:
1. Drop the constant-vs-dynamic ATT dimension, which gives identical coverage. Replace it with AR(1) error persistence, rho in {0, 0.8}. That is the only setting where SA's omitted covariance lowers coverage; under iid errors the omission makes SA conservative at e=2.
2. Use fixed, equal cohort counts. Then CS and SA point estimates coincide, and the headline SA diagnostic can be the per-replication paired ratio se_SA / se_CS_joint by e. Report both signs: 1.23-1.51 at e=2 iid, 0.93-0.96 at e=4,5 with rho=0.8. Keep se/MC-s.d. only as a secondary panel with its MC error shown.
3. Frame "cluster counts" as the number of never-treated units: 5 controls (8% of N=60) gives CS pointwise coverage of 0.755-0.87 and se/MC-s.d. of 0.80-0.88; 14 controls (N=180) recovers to 0.84-0.895. This is the dominant failure, and it is bigger than the SA effect.
4. Replace the tautological "simultaneous <= min pointwise" assert. Build a real sup-t band with supt_band(method='bootstrap', draws=event-study draws for e=0..5) and assert its coverage is within 3 MC s.e. of 0.90 (measured 0.900). Call the all-pointwise-intervals-cover frequency "joint coverage of pointwise bands".
5. Library (preferred, small): add bootstrap draws (event-study and overall) or an overall_ci/vcov to CallawaySantannaResult at callaway_santanna.py:196-258. Have sun_abraham reuse them instead of re-running CS and use them for a joint se. Fix the comment at sun_abraham.py:108-110. Without this change, keep the nested bootstrap at R≈100 and catch the no-control ValueError by redrawing.
6. For honest_did, either pass sigma from at least about 400 joint draws or present the diag(se^2) default at sensitivity.py:1229 as a demonstrated caveat. The pre-trend arm is still worth keeping: pointwise, sup-t and overall coverage fall to 0.01-0.14, and M=0 restores 0.82-0.90.
7. Scope to about 4 main cells (rho × {5, 15} controls) at R=200 plus one R=100 pre-trend/nested arm. Keep BJS out of the loop (1.6-3.2 s per call). lp_did at 4 ms is an optional third estimator with analytic cluster se.
8. Leave the pre-trend arm out of the unbiasedness assert and use a Bonferroni-style threshold of at least 3.5 MC s.e. over the 12 (e, estimator) tests. In "Your turn", assert only quantities that hold for every advertised N and never-treated share, not coverage levels.

All 7 symbols exist at the stated lines: callaway_santanna.py:350, sun_abraham.py:30, borusyak_jaravel_spiess.py:118, sensitivity.py:1035 (honest_did), lp_did.py:165, inference/supt.py:83, longrun/_job.py:321 (chunked). runtime.fit is at runtime/budget.py:207. I ran smoke calls on each in scratch wf/did-coverage-lab/timing.py, and all worked.

Native timings disagree with the proposal. CS(n_boot=100)+SA(n_boot=100) took 125-140 ms per replication in the MC loops at N=60 and N=180, against the claimed ~90 ms, because sun_abraham.py:88 re-runs the whole CS bootstrap. The nested B=99 whole-unit bootstrap took 0.28-0.35 s. Each honest_did call took about 0.11-0.17 s (0.35 s cold). lp_did took 4 ms. BJS(n_boot=100) took 1.6-3.2 s per call, so it cannot sit inside the MC loop.

supt_band(method='bootstrap', draws=...) works, but only on draws from the nested bootstrap. CS computes boot_es/boot_gt (callaway_santanna.py:196-203) and then throws them away. honest_did(result=cs) runs, but _extract_frame (sensitivity.py:875-890) supplies only the se column, so sigma = diag(se^2) (sensitivity.py:1229-1230). It also warns in every replication that the plug-in Delta^SD identified set is empty.
vets.oracle_check:
The simulation-truth oracle holds: the ATT is planted and coverage MC s.e. = sqrt(p(1-p)/R). My runs (scratch mc_main.py, R=200; mc_nested.py, R=150), all N=60 with 25% never-treated unless noted:
- Base cell, iid errors: CS pointwise 0.86-0.895, SA 0.87-0.93; joint coverage of the pointwise bands CS 0.535, SA 0.63. This matches the proposal's prototype.
- Nested arm: overall-ATT 90% coverage 0.873 (MC s.e. 0.027). A sup-t band built with supt_band on the nested draws covered 0.900 (0.024).
- Linear pre-trend arm (0.05 per period): coverage collapses (overall 0.03-0.05, sup-t 0.05-0.14). honest_did at M=0 restores 0.82-0.90.

Four problems with the proposed checks:
(1) The assert "simultaneous coverage <= min pointwise" is a tautology, not an oracle, and that frequency is not sup-t coverage.
(2) Reported SA se against MC s.d. is too noisy at R=200 (about 5% relative MC error on an s.d.). The effect under test is only 4-7%.
(3) Constant ATT and dynamic ATT give identical errors, bands and se to 3e-16 (scratch invariance.py), so the ATT-path dimension adds nothing.
(4) Under notebook 10's iid-error DGP, the omitted cross-cohort covariance is zero except where periods overlap (e=2), and there it is negative. SA se is therefore conservative there: the paired se_SA/se_CS was 1.23 with 25% never-treated and 1.51 with 8%. SA only undercovers with persistent errors. At rho=0.8 the ratio is 0.96/0.945 at e=4,5, and 0.93 at N=180 with 8% never-treated, which is about a 1-2 pp coverage loss and undetectable at R=200.

The fix: with equal cohort counts, CS and SA event-study points coincide (max diff 3e-16), so CS's joint-bootstrap se is the exact paired oracle for the SA se. Its MC s.e. is 0.005-0.02.
vets.data_check:
Synthetic only: a vectorised version of the notebook-10 DGP (notebooks/10_staggered_did.py:111-129: T=14, cohorts 5/8/11 plus never-treated, sigma 0.3, unit and time FE). No fetch and no licensing issue. The claimed seeded miss is confirmed from the executed notebooks/10_staggered_did.ipynb output: "CS overall ATT = +1.129 (90% unit-bootstrap CI [+1.020, +1.252])", truth +1.000.

Two DGP choices needed. Notebook 10 assigns cohorts at random (line 118), which makes SA and CS diverge and can leave zero never-treated units: P = 0.92^60 ≈ 0.7% at 8% of N=60. Use fixed, equal cohort counts. In the nested bootstrap, a resample with no never-treated units raises ValueError (callaway_santanna.py:163-167). With 5 controls that is about 0.5% of draws, roughly 50 per 100×99 run, so redraw on failure.

vets.oracle_check:
The planted ATT path is truth independent of puremacro, and the MC s.e. sqrt(p(1-p)/R) is standard, so the oracle is sound and obtainable. No published table is needed or claimed.

A stronger oracle exists and should be added. In notebook 10's DGP the unit and time fixed effects cancel exactly, so ATT_hat(g,e)-ATT = mean_treated(de) - mean_ctrl(de) is exactly Gaussian with closed-form moments:
- Var = [2g(0)-2g(e+1)](1/n_g+1/n_c).
- Cross-cohort Cov at the same e with D=g'-g is [2g(D)-g(|D-1-e|)-g(D+e+1)]/n_c.
This gives the exact sd of every SA, CS and overall estimate for comparison with the reported se.

The closed form is checked against my MC. With iid errors the covariance is zero except at e=D-1=2, where it is -s^2/n_c; predicted corr -0.39 at N=60/8%, MC -0.39/-0.45.

That closed form refutes the proposal's premise for its own grid. Under notebook 10's iid DGP the SA diagonal formula is conservative, not anti-conservative:
- SA se/sd is 1.20-1.37 at e=2 and 0.93-0.97 elsewhere.
- SA coverage at e=2 is 0.95-0.98.
- The 8% never-treated cell only deepens the negative correlation (-0.43).
Positive shared-control covariance appears only with persistence. At rho=0.8 and 8% never-treated, corr at e=4,5 was +0.10 to +0.27, SA se/sd 0.85-0.91 and coverage 0.81-0.87.

The asserted identity "simultaneous <= min pointwise" is a tautology for joint coverage of the pointwise intervals, which is what the prototype's 0.48-0.66 measures (I got 0.41-0.67). It is false in general for a real sup-t band.

ideas.title: Coverage lab: HAR fixed-b/EWC size, pointwise vs sup-t IRF bands, bootstrap coverage near a unit root, with Monte Carlo standard errors
ideas.anchor_notebook: new lab (09-20 review 'uncertainty/coverage lab'); also fix macro_history_and_climate/N12_paleoclimate_eiv_and_simex
ideas.question: Across persistent regressors, IRF horizons, measurement error and many tests, which interval procedures keep their nominal coverage?
ideas.description: This is a set of Monte Carlo exercises with a known truth. (a) HAR inference: Newey-West with the default bandwidth against LLSW fixed-b (hac_fixed_b, llsw_critical_value) as regressor persistence rises. The tabulated critical values are checked by simulating the Kiefer-Vogelsang fixed-b limit. (b) Joint coverage of LP IRFs: pointwise bands against supt_band. (c) Bootstraps: wild_bootstrap, block_bootstrap, moving_block_bootstrap and cum_irf_block_bootstrap against the analytic SE. (d) Errors in variables: OLS attenuation and simex_ols. N12 hand-rolls SIMEX with regress.ols in N12:75-123 instead of calling it. (e) Specification search: multipletests and fdrcorrection family-wise and FDR control. (f) Panel diagnostics: pesaran_cd, swamy_test and quandt_andrews_supF size and power. (g) Heteroskedasticity-based identification: lewbel_iv recovers beta when the Lewbel conditions hold and fails when they do not.
ideas.oracle_detail: Known DGP parameters and nominal coverage rates. The fixed-b limit distribution simulated from Brownian-motion functionals, independent of the _LLSW_CV table at puremacro/inference/hac_fixed_b.py:20-45, which cites 'LLSW (2018) Table 2' but has not been checked against the paper.
ideas.data_detail: Seeded simulations only. Keep replications small (a few hundred) so the notebook runs in Pyodide.
ideas.library_gaps: The hac_fixed_b docstring says hac_fixed_b(u, X, b) but the signature is (y, X, b). Check the LLSW table against the paper before teaching from it. No gap otherwise.
ideas.plan_overlap: This is the 09-20 review's 'uncertainty/coverage lab'. Notebook 20 (unit roots with power) is the nearest existing notebook. Every inference symbol listed has 0 notebook call sites today.

Simulation truth is independent and cheap. Two published targets also exist; I read both in this session from PDFs fetched with Python.
1. LLSW 2018, Table 1 (discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10160486/1/har_JBES_v8.pdf, printed p.35). 5% null rejection rates at T=200, x and u independent AR(1) with coefficient sqrt(rho), for rho=0.3/0.5/0.7:

- EWC with nu=0.4T^(2/3): 0.062/0.071/0.097
My library replication: 0.091/0.116/0.181, 0.071/0.080/0.109 and 0.067/0.070/0.092, with MC s.e. 0.006-0.009. All within about 1 s.e.
2. Kiefer-Vogelsang 2005, Table I, Bartlett kernel (cae.economics.cornell.edu/05-08.pdf, printed p.24). 95%/97.5% quantiles: b=0.1 1.861/2.235; b=0.2 2.081/2.553; b=0.3 2.324/2.878; b=0.5 2.781/3.514; b=1.0 3.764/4.771.
The proposal suspected the library table; it is wrong. _LLSW_CV (hac_fixed_b.py:23-48) gives, for two-sided alpha 0.10/0.05: b=0.2 1.93/2.32; b=0.3 2.04/2.46; b=0.5 2.30/2.83; b=1 3.05/3.96. My simulated fixed-b limit (T=1000, R=40000, library bandwidth convention) agrees with KV: b=0.5 2.745/3.467; b=1 3.771/4.770.
Size when the library values are used: b=0.2 gives 0.070 at nominal 5%; b=0.5 gives 0.092 at 5%; b=1 gives 0.162 at 10%. At b=0.05 the test under-rejects (0.085 at 10%). The citation is also wrong: LLSW Table 2 (printed p.36) is 'Constants in loss-minimizing rules for b' (b0 and nu0), not critical values. The table is close to KV only near b=0.1, which is why the LLSW-rule replication at T=200 still works.

ideas.title: Information-set lab and rebuild of 33: leaked fit vs holdout vs release-calendar backtest, with exact Bańbura-Modugno news on real vintages
ideas.question: How much does a nowcast's apparent accuracy depend on whether the target quarter's GDP, and data released after the decision date, enter estimation?
ideas.description: Rebuild 33 on its planted two-factor DGP. Compute three versions of the same nowcast: (a) the current leaked bridge (the target in the fit), (b) the target held out as in 48, and (c) a pseudo-real-time backtest over many target quarters using only observations released by each decision date. Report RMSE against a training-mean benchmark and against the infeasible oracle nowcast from the true factors, and keep the Bańbura-Modugno news identity. Connects 34, 48 and 59.
ideas.oracle_detail: The DGP is known (gdp = 2.2 + 1.4*F_q + noise, 33.py:89), so the infeasible nowcast from the true factors gives the error floor. The news decomposition must close to 1e-10.
ideas.data_detail: Seeded simulation inside the notebook; no external data.
ideas.library_gaps: nowcast_gdp always fits the bridge on every quarter with finite GDP (dfm_nowcast.py:355-366); an exclude_target flag, or at least a warning when the target quarter has GDP, would stop the leak.
ideas.plan_overlap: Implements the 'information-set lab' in REVIEW.md:134-137; not in PLAN.md.

vets.required_changes:
1. Replace 33.py:86-90. Generate GDP from quarterly averages of F_true plus eps (sigma 0.3), and extend the sample to at least 240 months. Define the oracle as mu + b'·Fbar_true and report its RMSE as the floor.

2. Build the lab as a grid: {leaked in-sample fit, same panel with target GDP in the bridge, pseudo-real-time} × decision month {1, 2, 3} × n_factors {2, 5} × training length {short, long}, over at least 20 seeds, against the training mean and the oracle.
   - Headline: leaked beats the oracle (0.258 vs 0.298) while honest is 0.570.
   - Also say plainly that with K=2 and a long sample the leak is small (0.339 vs 0.384).
   - Add diebold_mariano for honest vs benchmark.

3. Remove "keep the B-M identity" and rewrite 33:136-148. Label nowcast_gdp's table as a same-vintage residual and show its contributions sum to about 0. Add exact news through banbura_modugno_news on a raw StateSpaceModel: companion transition with 3 factor lags and a GDP row beta/3·[I I I], parameters fit on the old vintage only, one released month plus one revised past value, asserting decomposition_error < 1e-10. Do not put quarterly GDP into DynamicFactorModel as a column. State that the news nowcast is the Kalman-bridge estimator, not the EM-PCA number.

4. Drop realtime_nowcast from the capability list, or fix it first (fit on the old vintage, keep a real nowcast history).

5. Take the ALFRED real-vintage half and the labs-6 K=8 release/first-vs-final DGP out of this rebuild. Make them a follow-up that needs a small bundled public-domain vintage fixture with FRED attribution, or put them in 38.

6. Library (small, optional): exclude_target=True or a warning in nowcast_gdp (dfm_nowcast.py:355); a mixed-frequency guard or error in DynamicFactorModel.fit when complete-case rows are not contiguous (dfm.py:418).

vets.oracle_check:
As proposed, the oracle is mis-specified. At 33.py:88-89, F_q is the cross-sectional mean of the observed panel's quarterly means (idiosyncratic noise and ragged-edge NaNs included). It is not the true factors: corr(F_q, Fbar_true[:,0]) = 0.96 and with F2 0.44. A "nowcast from the true factors" is therefore not the DGP's conditional mean.

Fix: generate gdp = mu + b'·quarterly-mean(F_true) + eps. The oracle is then mu + b'·Fbar_true, with RMSE ≈ sigma_eps; the smoke test gave 0.297-0.306 for sigma = 0.3. With that fix the oracle works well and flags leakage. Example: with 5 factors and fewer than 16 training quarters, the leaked RMSE of 0.258 beats the infeasible oracle (0.298), while the honest pseudo-real-time RMSE is 0.570.

The news identity check is a sound internal-consistency oracle, but only for a Kalman state-space nowcast. It does not cover the EM-PCA number from nowcast_gdp. The training-mean benchmark works (RMSE about 2.0-2.3).

vets.capabilities_check:
Every named symbol exists and is exported (puremacro/nowcast/__init__.py:21-40), but two of them do not do what the proposal assumes.
(1) nowcast_gdp (dfm_nowcast.py:192) is enough for parts (a), (b) and (c). GDP never enters the EM-PCA step, so the leaked and held-out fits have identical factors (measured max|dF| = 0.0). The bridge keeps only quarters with finite GDP (dfm_nowcast.py:355), so passing s_gdp.iloc[:-1] (as 48:120 does) removes the leak. No exclude_target flag is needed; a warning at :355 would be an optional guardrail.
(2) "Keep the BM news identity" is a false premise. 33's news panel is nowcast_gdp's single-vintage projection table (dfm_nowcast.py:380-398), not Bańbura-Modugno, and it closes no identity; 48:20,31 already says so. 33.py:24 wrongly calls it "exact news attribution".
(3) banbura_modugno_news (news.py:161) needs a state space that contains the target. With DynamicFactorModel and GDP as a panel column, the identity closes (measured 2.5e-15), but the model is misspecified in two ways. fit() runs PCA and the factor VAR only on complete-case rows (dfm.py:418,434); with quarterly GDP those are the quarter-end months, so a quarter-spaced VAR is used as a monthly one. There is also no 3-month aggregation of GDP. In a measured month-3 backtest (T=240, 40 quarters) its GDP nowcast had RMSE 1.01, against 0.32 for the bridge. mf_var does have the Mariano-Murasawa aggregation (mfvar.py:163-178) and returns A, Q, Z and H for a StateSpaceModel, but it has no intercept or demeaning, and this route is untested.
(4) realtime_nowcast is unsuitable for this lab. It fits on the latest vintage (realtime_nowcast.py:417-421), and its vintage_history column "nowcast" is really the last published target value (:471-474), not a model nowcast.
vets.oracle_check:
The simulation-truth oracle is obtainable, but the proposal describes it wrongly. 33's GDP loads on F_q, the cross-sectional mean of the observed indicators X (33.py:88), not on the true factors F_true. The correct infeasible oracle is therefore E[gdp | complete X] = 2.2 + 1.4*F_q, with an error floor equal to the noise s.d., 0.3 (33.py:89). Measured oracle RMSE was 0.28-0.34 across seeds. A regression on the true-factor means gives 0.32 in-sample, but it is not the DGP's conditional mean.
DGP flaw: 33.py:84 masks the last month before 33.py:88 builds F_q, so the target quarter's "truth" depends on the publication mask. GDP must be generated from the complete panel before masking.
There is also a stronger oracle that does not depend on puremacro: the leave-one-out (PRESS) identity. Because the leaked and held-out fits share the same factors, the leaked error equals (1 - h_TT) times the held-out error. Measured in the notebook-33 configuration: gap 5.6e-16, h_TT = 0.105, leaked error -0.612 vs held-out -0.684. It can be checked with numpy lstsq alone.
If a BM identity is kept, the 1e-10 check is only internal consistency, not an independent oracle. No published table is involved, so none was needed.
vets.data_check:
Synthetic data is adequate, and the proposal contradicts itself: the title says "on real vintages" while data_status is synthetic.
The ALFRED half from cov-ts-2 would need network access or a new monthly vintage fixture. The only ALFRED file in the repo, notebooks/course/data/alfred_pib_primeras_publicaciones.csv, has 6 GDP release rows, which is not a monthly panel. Drop that half here; it belongs with 38 and the repl-emp-13 cluster.
The sample is too small. 33 uses T=72 months (24 quarters), which leaves about 12 evaluation quarters. Measured results with T=240: 68 evaluation quarters in about 2 s; T=480 takes 4 s. Both are fine for Pyodide.
vets.novelty_check:
Only partly novel.
Part (b), the held-out target, is already done in 48:117-121, which also explains the difference between the projection table and BM news (48:20,31). The BM identity at 1e-10 is already asserted in 59:207,217,331 through realtime_nowcast, so cov-ts-2's claim that "59 never calls it" is wrong in substance. The multi-quarter backtest appears only as unimplemented stretch prompts in 48:386 and 34:241. Notebook 19 (19:70-147) runs a pseudo-out-of-sample race, but for unemployment, not a nowcast.
The ITAM course already has part (c) on real FRED data. curso/notebooks/T01_C_high_frequency.ipynb §4 (cells 28-33) runs an expanding-window, after-month-1/2/3 nowcast backtest over 80 quarters (2000Q1-2019Q4) with a DFM ragged-edge bridge and MIDAS, against mean, AR(1) and AR(2), and it does the bridge by hand because nowcast_gdp's target_quarter is only a label.
PLAN.md contains nothing on nowcasting.
What is new is the three-way comparison of leaked fit, holdout and release calendar, with a known oracle, per-series release lags and the PRESS identity. That is exactly the REVIEW.md:134-137 lab, and it fixes 33, which REVIEW.md:124-125 flagged. The duplicate script puremacro/examples/nowcasting_gdp_news.py:57 has the same leak.

ideas.title: Grading density forecasts: PIT, Berkowitz, CRPS, log scores and the forecast-combination puzzle
ideas.anchor_notebook: 19_model_confidence_set (extends its DM/MCS point-forecast view to densities)
ideas.question: How do you tell a well-calibrated predictive density from a sharp but wrong one, and why do equal combination weights so often beat estimated ones?
ideas.description: Part A, Monte Carlo on known DGPs: draw correct, over-dispersed, under-dispersed and biased Gaussian predictives. Compute pit, pit_histogram (the U or inverted-U shapes), pit_uniformity_test and berkowitz_test rejection rates against nominal size. Show crps_ensemble converging to the closed-form crps_gaussian as the ensemble size M grows. Part B, recursive pseudo-out-of-sample on bundled inflation and GDP growth: a constant-variance AR, AR-GARCH (garch11_fit) and optionally bvar_sv, ranked by log score (klic_amisano_giacomini) and conditionally by giacomini_white. Part C, the combination puzzle: equal_weight versus inverse_mse, bates_granger and rank_weight when the true optimal weights are known, and a Brier score for a recession-probability forecast. Cross-check the duplicate implementations (forecast.density versus nowcast.scoring) against each other.
ideas.paper: Diebold, Gunther & Tay (1998); Berkowitz (2001); Gneiting & Raftery (2007); Amisano & Giacomini (2007); Giacomini & White (2006); Bates & Granger (1969); Smith & Wallis (2009)
ideas.oracle_detail: Rejection frequencies under a known correct density against nominal 5%, and power under known misspecification. Closed-form Gaussian CRPS: validation/cases_forecast.py:78 uses the stdlib-erf reference, and :205 pins crps0 = sqrt(2/pi) - 1/sqrt(pi). Known optimal Bates-Granger weights in the combination DGP. vets.oracle_check:
Simulation truth is sound, with one false claim.

The claim is that the forecast and nowcast CRPS/PIT implementations 'must agree numerically'. That holds only for crps_gaussian (identical). crps_ensemble differs by design (fair vs M^2), with an exact analytic gap of sigma/(M sqrt(pi)), because E|X-X'| = 2 sigma/sqrt(pi). The observed gap was 0.0558 at M=10 against a predicted 0.0564. The PIT conventions differ by O(1/sqrt(M)): the max gap against the exact CDF was 0.11 at M=200. So the correct oracle is: the fair estimator is unbiased for the closed form, the M^2 estimator's bias equals sigma/(M sqrt(pi)), and the two Berkowitz likelihoods agree to a stated tolerance.

The Bates-Granger oracle works, from my own Monte Carlo (500 reps):
- w* = Sigma^-1 1/(1'Sigma^-1 1) = [0.453, 0.280, 0.267], giving MSE* = 0.7545 against 0.7667 for equal weights.
- Out of sample with a training window R=20: BG 0.845, equal 0.768, inverse-MSE 0.771, rank 0.793, oracle 0.757.
- At R=400: BG 0.755 and equal 0.763. The puzzle appears and then reverses as R grows.

The proposal's risk statement is misattributed. With known densities, KS and Berkowitz are correctly sized even at T=50 (5.4% and 5.0%). Size distortion comes from estimated parameters in recursive pseudo-out-of-sample runs and from dependence at h>1. Calibrated h=2 forecasts are rejected 100% by the 3-df Berkowitz test and 13% by KS (T=200, 1000 reps).

No published table values are needed or were used.

vets.oracle_check:
The oracle is independent and obtainable, but three claims need correcting.
(a) The CRPS reference: GR2007 was fetched this session (sites.stat.washington.edu/raftery/Research/PDF/Gneiting2007jasa.pdf, text via pypdf). It defines CRPS as eq. (20), gives the kernel form E|X-x| - 1/2 E|X-X'| as eq. (21), and prints the Gaussian closed form unnumbered right after (21). Its eq. (5) is a general expected-score relation and its eq. (27) is a Dawid-Sebastiani-type score. The paper contains no M(M-1) 'fair' ensemble estimator. So forecast/density.py:58 ('eq. 27') and validation/cases_forecast.py:194, :208 ('eq. (5)') and :222 ('eq. (27) fair estimator') mis-cite it. crps0 = sqrt(2/pi) - 1/sqrt(pi) is correct (2*phi(0) = sqrt(2/pi)). A better oracle than the stdlib-erf re-derivation, which is the same formula, is scipy.integrate.quad of definition (20). I checked it at three points and it matches crps_gaussian to about 1e-15.
(b) GR2007 (same text) says the CRPS equals the integral of Brier scores over all thresholds. That gives an independent check linking brier_score to crps_gaussian: 0.35240 vs 0.35252 on a trapezoid grid.
(c) 'Both implementations must agree numerically' is false for ensembles. The right oracle is the analytic bias of the M^2 estimator, E|X-X'|/(2M) = sigma/(M*sqrt(pi)). Measured bias was 0.117, 0.063, 0.008 and 0.003 against theory 0.113, 0.056, 0.011 and 0.003 at M = 5, 10, 50, 200.
(d) Size and power: the known DGP plus the asymptotic chi2(3) is simulation truth independent of puremacro. Measured size (R=1000): T=50 KS 0.046 and Berkowitz 0.041; T=100 0.063/0.061; T=250 0.051/0.055. Power at T=100 (R=500): sd 0.7 gives KS 0.53 vs Berkowitz 0.99; sd 1.4 gives 0.40 vs 0.99; bias 0.3 gives 0.72 vs 0.69. For a closed-form power benchmark, a local noncentral-chi2 approximation with lambda = T[mu^2 + (s_z^2-1)^2/2] is available. Berkowitz's own Monte Carlo is not a usable target. I fetched FEDS 1999-11 (federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/1999/199911/199911pap.pdf), the working-paper version of the JBES article. Its Table 1 uses Black-Scholes option portfolios, not Gaussian predictives, so it could only be a stretch exercise.
(e) Combination: the optimal weights w* = S^-1 1/(1'S^-1 1) and the population MSE w'Sw are exact. Smith & Wallis (2009, OBES 71(3):331-355, RePEc abstract fetched) confirms the finite-sample weight-estimation explanation.

ideas.title: Forecast-comparison pitfalls lab: look-ahead tuning, overlapping errors, nested-model DM size, Clark-West, GW and fluctuation tests
ideas.question: When does a forecast comparison lie: leaked tuning, overlapping h-step errors, nested models, or wrong critical values?
ideas.description: Five parts on DGPs whose truth is known. (a) Look-ahead: AR(p) and penalized forecasts of a planted AR/factor DGP. Choose the lag order (lag_select) or penalty (forecast_penalized) on the full sample, then again inside each rolling training window. Compare in-sample, leaked out-of-sample and honest out-of-sample RMSE against a training-mean benchmark; R=200. (b) Overlap: two forecasts with equal population MSE whose h-step errors are MA(h-1). Run diebold_mariano with small_sample=True (HLN) and False on the grid h in {1,4,8} x T in {40,80,160}, R=2000 per cell. Prototype sizes at nominal 5%: h=1 0.040-0.053; h=4 HLN 0.074-0.082, normal 0.086-0.131; h=8 HLN 0.088-0.093, normal 0.118-0.194. (c) Fixed-b: a DM t-stat via hac_fixed_b on the loss differential, with critical values taken both from llsw_critical_value and from simulation. (d) Nested models: AR vs AR plus an irrelevant predictor under the null; DM vs giacomini_white. (e) model_confidence_set: how often the MCS contains the true best model (R=100, n_boot=500). Runtime: DM is 0.07 ms per call; parts b-c take about 15 s natively (vectorised FFT for c); part e is untimed and must be budgeted before it goes in. Figure: size curves by T for each h and test; bars of look-ahead optimism (leaked/honest RMSE); MCS inclusion frequency. Exercise: choose h and T. Assert that HLN size <= normal-DM size in the MC and that leaked RMSE <= honest RMSE on average.
ideas.paper: Diebold and Mariano (1995); Harvey, Leybourne and Newbold (1997); Clark and McCracken (2001); Giacomini and White (2006); Hansen, Lunde and Nason (2011); Lazarus, Lewis, Stock and Watson (2018); Coroneo and Iacone (2020)
ideas.oracle_detail: The equal-accuracy null holds by construction, so every rejection is a size error; MC s.e. is sqrt(0.05*0.95/R). For part c the oracle is the simulated null distribution of the implemented statistic. This session found (T=1000, R=8000, iid N(0,1)) 95% |t| quantiles of 2.10, 2.25, 2.55, 2.86, 3.53 and 4.65 at b=0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5 and 1.0. The tabulated llsw_critical_value gives 2.16, 2.21, 2.32, 2.46, 2.83 and 3.96. An FFT reimplementation matched hac_fixed_b's t to 6e-15.
ideas.data_detail: Simulated AR/factor DGPs and MA(h-1) error pairs; no files.
ideas.library_gaps: (1) BUG candidate: the fixed-b critical-value table in puremacro/inference/hac_fixed_b.py:23-47 (docstring source: 'LLSW (2018), Table 2') is too small for b>=0.2 relative to the simulated distribution of the statistic that hac_fixed_b computes. It over-rejects: at b=0.5 the nominal 5% value is 2.83 against a simulated 3.53. Audit the table against the paper, which this session did not read, before the lab teaches it. (2) There is no Clark-West or Clark-McCracken test for nested models. (3) diebold_mariano fixes the Bartlett bandwidth at h-1 (compare.py:43-49), with no option for another bandwidth or fixed-b.
ideas.plan_overlap: Not in PLAN.md. 19 teaches the MCS on real data without size experiments. 34 and 48 fixed information leaks in single examples. This lab generalises those corrections.

Simulation truth is valid for every part, but two parts expose library bugs rather than econometrics.

(b) puremacro's HLN-DM does not converge to 5% as T grows (R=2000, equal-MSE MA(h-1) errors, scratch sims.py and sims2.py):
- h=4, T=40/80/160/400/1000: 0.075/0.074/0.088/0.092/0.082.
- h=8, same T: 0.086/0.078/0.102/0.084/0.095.
- A Bartlett estimator with fixed L=h-1 is inconsistent for the long-run variance of an MA(h-1) loss differential.
- The rectangular h-1 estimator with HLN gives h=4: 0.072/0.056/0.057 and h=8: 0.108/0.073/0.074 at T=40/80/160.
- Sources read this session: ForeComp (Shin and Schor, arXiv 2603.07458, eq. 5-6 and Table 1) states that DM uses a rectangular kernel truncated at h-1 and that HLN applies to it. R forecast DM2.R:95-101 uses the unweighted "acf" estimator by default; its non-default "bartlett" option (weights 1-k/h) is exactly puremacro's estimator.
- So the proposal's prototype sizes (h=4 HLN 0.074-0.082, h=8 0.088-0.093) mostly measure puremacro's kernel choice, not an HLN small-sample limit.
- The planned assertion "HLN size <= normal size" holds by construction in every replication (factor < 1 and t critical value > z), so it tests nothing.

(c) The proposal's oracle is confirmed and now also matches a published formula. ForeComp eq. (10) quotes the Kiefer-Vogelsang (2005) Bartlett 97.5% quantile as 1.9600 + 2.9694b + 0.4160b^2 - 0.5324b^3.
- KV formula at b = .05/.1/.2/.3/.5/1: 2.109/2.261/2.566/2.874/3.482/4.813.
- My simulation (T=1000, R=8000): 2.11/2.26/2.57/2.88/3.49/4.76.
- The table (hac_fixed_b.py:26-46): 2.16/2.21/2.32/2.46/2.83/3.96.
- Actual size at nominal 5% using the table: 0.045/0.053/0.072/0.085/0.097/0.091.
- The 10% entries are also wrong: at b=0.5 the simulated value is 2.80 against 2.30 in the table.
- LLSW (2018) itself was not read (UCL returned 403).

(a) The look-ahead premise holds, but the gap is small. Prototype: AR(3), T=200, rolling window 80, 120 out-of-sample points, 60 reps, sims2.py.

(d) Nested null (AR(1) vs AR(1) plus an irrelevant x, R=500, sims3.py), rolling / recursive:

ideas.title: FRED-MD factors: Bai-Ng counts against McCracken-Ng, diffusion-index forecasts (Stock-Watson 2002) and a FAVAR
ideas.question: Does puremacro's factor machinery reproduce McCracken and Ng's factor count and variance shares on a frozen FRED-MD vintage?
ideas.description: Promote puremacro/examples/dfm_bai_ng.py (synthetic, k=2 recovered). Steps: download a frozen FRED-MD vintage; apply the tcode transforms and the outlier rule; estimate factors (EM for gaps); report the IC and PC tables, the marginal R2 of each factor and the top-loading series. Add a math cell on the IC_p and PC_p penalties and an exercise comparing vintages and the effect of outlier adjustment. Links to notebooks 33 and 34 (diffusion-index forecasting).
ideas.paper: Bai and Ng (2002) Econometrica; McCracken and Ng (2016) JBES
ideas.oracle_detail: McCracken and Ng, St. Louis Fed WP 2015-012B (Aug 2015), read this session from the PDF: 'The PCp2 criterion finds r = 8 factors' (nine without outlier adjustment); factor 1 explains 0.159 and the eight factors 0.476 of total variation in 134 series; on the earlier GSI vintages PCp2 finds 8 factors (2003, 2007, 2011) and 7 (2013).
ideas.data_detail: FRED-MD historical vintage CSVs from the St. Louis Fed (for example 2015-08, to match the WP). Freeze the vintage with its tcode row.
ideas.library_gaps: bai_ng_ic (puremacro/factor.py:75-117) implements IC_p1-3 only, not the PC_p2 criterion McCracken and Ng use. There is no EM algorithm for an unbalanced panel or missing values, no FRED-MD tcode transform or outlier helper, and no marginal-R2 table.
ideas.plan_overlap: Not in PLAN.md.

vets.oracle_check: I read the oracle this session from s3.amazonaws.com/real.stlouisfed.org/wp/2015/2015-012.pdf (WP 2015-012B, 'Revision Date August 2015'), pp.7-8 and Table 1 p.19. The PCp2 penalty is (N+T)/(NT)·log min(N,T). 'The PCp2 criterion finds r = 8 factors', and nine without outlier adjustment. Table 1 mR2(1..8) = .159 .069 .066 .051 .041 .036 .029 .024, with a total of 0.476. The earlier GSI vintages give 8/8/8/7. The proposal's vintage is wrong: the paper uses the 2015:04 vintage, sample 1960:3-2014:12, T=658 ('1959:1-2015:04 with 675 observations'), not 2015-08. I reproduced it with EM-PCA plus PCp2 on 2015-04.csv, T=658 and N=133. mR2 came out .163 .070 .065 .054 .043 .036 .027 .026, total 0.484. Top loaders: F1 USGOOD .742 (paper .749), PAYEMS .723 (.731), MANEMP .700 (.703), NAPM .656 (.658). F2 T10YFFM .595 (.613). F3 CUSR0000SAC .691 (.730). So the oracle is reachable within about 0.005 on mR2(k), 0.01 on the total and 0.05 on per-series R2. The factor count, however, depends on kmax, and the paper never states kmax. With outlier adjustment PCp2 gives r=8 at kmax 8-9, 9 at kmax 10 and 11 at kmax 12/15. Without adjustment it gives 9 at kmax 9-10. The paper's '8, and 9 without outliers' holds exactly only at kmax=9. The GSI-vintage numbers cannot be checked because that data is not bundled or public in this form. A second oracle is available in the paper text: FRED-MD diffusion-index MSEs in Table 3 (IP h=1, post-1990: 35.74 with one factor vs 35.39 with two; h=12: 9.22 vs 11.20). SW 2002's own numbers use a different dataset and are not an oracle on FRED-MD.

ideas.title: Bayesian VARs: Minnesota prior, GLP marginal-likelihood tightness and calibrated fan charts
ideas.anchor_notebook: new (relates to notebooks/47_applied_central_bank_policy_suite.py, which builds fans from fit_var draws, and notebooks/19_model_confidence_set.py)
ideas.question: How much do a Minnesota prior and empirically chosen tightness improve density forecasts of US GDP growth, inflation and the policy rate, and are the resulting fans calibrated?
ideas.description: Merge five uncovered examples into one notebook: bvar_fan_chart, glp_lambda_search, posterior_predictive_fan, mcmc_diagnostics and gk_robust_from_gibbs (optional appendix). minnesota_gibbs is called by no notebook code. Add: a math cell on the Minnesota and NIW priors and the GLP marginal likelihood; a Gibbs-versus-closed-form check; a pseudo-out-of-sample evaluation with PIT, Berkowitz and CRPS; convergence diagnostics; an exercise that varies lambda1 and the sample length. The exercise tests the glp example's printed expectation, which currently fails: lambda1 stays at 0.2 for T=60 to 480.
ideas.paper: Litterman (1986); Giannone, Lenza and Primiceri (2015) REStat
ideas.oracle_detail: With a conjugate NIW prior the posterior moments and the marginal likelihood are closed form, so the Gibbs draws must match them within Monte Carlo error. A test of the glp claim ('expect optimal lambda_1 to relax', glp_lambda_search.py:58) comes free. The GLP (2015) published hyperparameters would be a second oracle (not read this session).
ideas.data_detail: FRED GDPC1, GDPDEF or PCEPI, and FEDFUNDS; freeze a vintage, or reuse a bundled quarterly macro file if its coverage suffices.
ideas.library_gaps: Confirm that minnesota_gibbs exposes a conjugate path whose marginal likelihood matches the GLP formula. minnesota_optimal_lambda searches a grid only (no GLP hyperpriors). The glp example's printed claim is unverified or false.
ideas.plan_overlap: Not in PLAN.md. Overlaps partly with the 09-20 uncertainty/coverage lab.

vets.required_changes:
1. Library first. Fix _build_minnesota_dummies (puremacro/var/bvar.py:241-253): one own-scaled row per (lag, variable) slot, prior mean in Yd, and lambda2 refused or warned for the conjugate path. Add an optional per-variable prior-mean vector delta, shared with minnesota_posterior and bvar_sv. Set the minnesota_optimal_lambda default lambda2_grid to (1.0,). Add tests for column-permutation invariance of log ML and the posterior mean, for log ML against the candidate/Chib identity, and for tight lambda1 driving the diagonal to delta.
2. Rename the check "direct Monte Carlo from the NIW posterior vs closed form" and make the Chib-identity log-ML check the headline oracle. Explain why the conjugate prior cannot hold lambda2: Kronecker structure, and bvar_sv's independent Normal prior as the fix.
3. Move convergence diagnostics (Gelman-Rubin, ESS, Geweke) to bvar_sv chains, which gave max R-hat 1.37 at 2x(300+300) draws on the real data. Drop or rewrite examples/mcmc_diagnostics.py's premise.
4. Turn the glp exercise into "lambda* converges, it does not grow". Show lambda1* against T with lambda2=1 on a fine grid (0.32 -> 0.25 -> 0.20 plateau), give the Laplace-approximation argument, and fix the text at glp_lambda_search.py:9-10 and :58.
5. Data: log levels of GDPC1, quarterly-average CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS from the bundled files. Do not use A191RL1Q225SBEA as inflation, and fix the loaders.py:117/:403 label. For the BGR growing-VAR point, use a 6-7 variable bundled panel (1971+). A 20-variable panel only goes in with a frozen FRED vintage.
6. Density evaluation: build PITs from the predictive ensemble ECDF and use crps_ensemble, not crps_gaussian. Report Berkowitz and KS. Expect and explain the miscalibration: over-dispersion and upward bias after 1984.
7. Add a homoskedastic-BVAR vs bvar_sv comparison on thinned origins, or freeze the long runs, and keep live runs to minnesota_gibbs (4 ms per fit).
8. Call the method "GLP-style grid empirical Bayes (flat hyperprior, no sum-of-coefficients or initial-observation priors)". Do not cite GLP-published hyperparameters unless they are read from the paper and the missing priors are added.
9. Keep the gk_robust_from_gibbs appendix optional and run it only after the fix.
vets.capabilities_check:
All seven symbols exist at the stated paths: minnesota_gibbs (puremacro/var/bvar.py:266), minnesota_optimal_lambda (bvar.py:467), simulate_var_paths (puremacro/posterior.py:14), fan_chart_quantiles (posterior.py:60), berkowitz_test (puremacro/forecast/density.py:182), crps_gaussian (density.py:41) and gelman_rubin (puremacro/mcmc.py:58). The smoke runs were in scratch wf/bvar-feas/smoke1-5.py. Four defects undercut the proposal as written.
(1) CONFIRMED BUG in _build_minnesota_dummies (bvar.py:243-252). The inner `for eq` loop overwrites Xd for each (lag, variable) slot, so the last equation's value wins. With lambda2 != 1, the implied prior mean on the own first lag becomes lambda2 for every variable except the last one. With the default lambda2=0.5 it is [0.5, 0.5, 1.0]. Those slots also get the cross-variable variance. The posterior depends on variable ordering: permuting columns changes log ML from -550.785 to -554.410 and moves A1 by up to 0.061. With lambda2=1 the result is order-invariant. minnesota_gibbs and _minnesota_log_marginal_likelihood both use this path, and the default grid in minnesota_optimal_lambda includes lambda2=0.5 (bvar.py:474).
(2) minnesota_gibbs is not a Gibbs sampler. It draws iid from the closed-form NIW posterior (bvar.py:340-346), and `burn` does nothing. Lag-1 ACF of the draws is -0.012, and R-hat is 1.001 at n=50. Its mean matches the closed-form B_post by construction, so the proposed "Gibbs vs closed form" check only tests the Monte Carlo sampler. Convergence diagnostics on it are vacuous. The docstring claim in examples/mcmc_diagnostics.py:10-11 ("small n_draws produces a marginal R-hat") is false.
(3) minnesota_posterior (equation by equation, own/cross prior, posterior mean only) implements a different prior from minnesota_gibbs. A1[0,0] is 0.589 vs 0.521 on the same data, and bvar_sv uses a third, independent-Normal prior.
(4) The own-lag prior mean is hard-coded at 1 in all three, with no per-variable delta option, so growth-rate variables cannot get the white-noise prior.
The rest works. The GLP log ML is correct for the prior the dummies imply: it equals the candidate/Chib identity log p(Y|th)+log p(th)-log p(th|Y) up to a lambda-invariant 0.0149, which comes from the 1e-8 ridge on Xd'Xd. simulate_var_paths accepts y_init of shape (p,n). crps_ensemble (density.py:57) exists and suits simulated predictives better than crps_gaussian. Genuine MCMC exists in bvar_sv (puremacro/var/bvar_sv.py:987), which has multi-chain R-hat and out-of-sample log_score. On real data it gave max R-hat 1.37 at 2x(300+300) draws, 0 stuck iterations and 2.6 s per fit. gk_robust_bands_from_gibbs exists (var/identify/sign_robust.py:142). Runtime is fine for Pyodide: minnesota_gibbs takes about 4 ms per fit, and a full 140-origin recursive OOS at 3 lambdas takes 2.7 s locally.
vets.oracle_check: "Gibbs draws match closed form" is a weak oracle. The draws come from that closed form, so the check only tests _inv_wishart and the Kronecker ordering, though it does pass (E[Sigma] diag 0.2539/0.2422/0.2375 closed form vs 0.2546/0.2422/0.2372 from draws). A stronger oracle is available and was verified: the basic marginal-likelihood (candidate/Chib) identity evaluated at the posterior mode with scipy invwishart plus a matrix-normal density. It reproduces _minnesota_log_marginal_likelihood to within a constant 0.0149 at (0.2,0.5,1), (0.1,1,1) and (1,1,2). A second oracle is the order-invariance check: permuting columns must leave log ML unchanged. It fails today when lambda2 != 1, so it doubles as the regression test for the bug fix. GLP (2015) published hyperparameters cannot serve as an oracle, and I did not read them this session. GLP's full procedure includes sum-of-coefficients tightness, which bvar.py:481-483 says is omitted, and the library has no dummy-initial-observation prior and no Gamma hyperpriors. The GLP-example claim is falsified. With lambda2=1, lambda3=1 and a 25-point geometric grid, lambda1* goes 0.316 (T=60) -> 0.251 (T=120) -> 0.200 for T=240-1920 across 3 seeds, so it tightens slightly and then plateaus instead of relaxing. That fits the Laplace argument: the lambda-dependent part of log ML tends to log p(theta0|lambda), so lambda* converges to a DGP-dependent constant. The shipped default grid returns lambda1=0.2, lambda2=0.5, lambda3=2 for every T in 60-480. lambda2=0.5 wins only because the bug moves the prior mean toward the DGP's 0.5-0.6 AR coefficients.
vets.data_check: The bundled series are enough offline. puremacro/datasets/data has GDPC1 (1947Q1-2026Q1), CPIAUCSL (monthly, 1947-01 to 2026-06) and FEDFUNDS (1954-07 to 2026-06). load_macro_quarterly (datasets/loaders.py:111) returns 1954Q3-2026Q1, 287 rows, but has no inflation series. loaders.py:117 and :403 mislabel A191RL1Q225SBEA as "GDP Deflator Inflation"; it is real GDP growth, and the loader names it gdp_growth_annualized. Build inflation from CPIAUCSL averaged to quarters, or fetch GDPDEF. Estimate in log levels (100*log GDP, 100*log CPI, FFR), since the own-lag prior mean is fixed at 1. A smoke run on 1954Q3-2019Q4 (262 obs), p=4, with lambda2=1 gave GLP-grid lambda1*=0.317. For the BGR "shrinkage as the VAR grows" extension, the bundled GPDIC1, CPILFESL, UNRATE and NFCI (from 1971) give 6-7 variables. A 20-variable panel needs fetch_fred (puremacro/fetch/_classic.py:50, network from Python only) and a frozen vintage committed as a fixture. FRED public series raise no licensing problem.
