Five problems the proposal missed, all verified by running code:
(1) The current notebook never nowcasts. 59.py:134 masks every series except gdp at the last month, so GDP is observed at the target period in both vintages. dfm.py:308 then returns the observed value (X_filled, set at dfm.py:447). The headline "nowcast" +100.6377 equals the simulated GDP value exactly, and its SD of 0.1123 has nothing to measure. The news decomposition covers a different quantity, the common component (100.5921 to 100.5976).
(2) Bug in realtime_nowcast.py:378-387: with as_of set, the previous vintage is all_vintages[-2] of the whole panel, which can be a later vintage. On a 24-vintage pseudo-real-time panel this gave an empty news table and an identity error of 1.1e-2 and 1.4e-2 (as_of = months 13 and 20). Passing previous_vintage explicitly restores an error of about 1e-14.
(3) The vintage_history block (realtime_nowcast.py:458-478) also ignores as_of and lists observed target values with a constant SD, not model nowcasts.
(4) The DFM's SD (realtime_nowcast.py:425-432) is a plug-in value that ignores parameter uncertainty. H comes from PCA residuals (dfm.py:429-431).
(5) The library has two Berkowitz implementations that disagree on the same PITs: the exact-likelihood one (evaluation.py:285-303) gives LR 1.356, the conditional-OLS one (forecast/density.py:182-228) gives 1.059. There is also a second pit_uniformity_test with the same name in forecast/density.py (KS only).
vets.oracle_check:
The oracle is obtainable but must be built separately. The proposal describes a true-DGP oracle and then computes PITs from the DFM, which is not the true density. I added a true-parameter Kalman arm (StateSpaceModel with the known loadings, Q=0.0625, H=0.0225, exact prior P0=0.0625) and ran a Monte Carlo on the notebook's DGP. Rejection rates at 5%:

| Setup | True density (LR / KS) | DFM own (LR / KS) | DFM × 0.6 (LR) | True × 0.6 (LR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T=36, 24 evaluation months, R=200 | 0.055 / 0.045 | 0.43 / 0.24 | 0.99 | 0.91 |

So Berkowitz has correct size and power; the DFM's own densities are not calibrated. The direction of the DFM's failure depends on the design:
- Random-walk DGP, T=120 (R=100): the DFM is over-dispersed (median var(z) 0.56, SD ratio 1.35), rejected 64% of the time. DFM × 0.6 is rejected only 69%.
- Random-walk DGP, T=60: rejected 28%.
- Stationary AR(1) factor DGP: consistently under-dispersed (var(z) about 1.4 to 1.5), rejected 25% to 31%.

Consequences:
- "The mis-scaled variant has a known direction of failure" holds only when the × 0.6 scaling is applied to the true density.
- "Parameter uncertainty ignored" is not a variant: the DFM baseline already ignores it.
- An assertion that the DFM passes on a single seed would be fragile, since the DFM is rejected in 25% to 64% of samples.
- The true arm should be a scalar Kalman filter written by hand in the notebook, so the oracle does not depend on puremacro.state_space.

ideas.question: What does each component of a policy-stance dashboard rest on (observed data, an illustrative corpus, an estimated posterior), and how do fan charts from a real posterior differ from ad hoc coefficient jitter?
ideas.description: Open with a provenance table: FRED data frozen on a stated date, a hand-written illustrative statement corpus (not official texts), and the model assumptions. Replace the N(0,0.015) jitter (47.py:275-278) with draws from a conjugate Minnesota/NIW posterior, compared with a residual bootstrap. Evaluate the fan chart's coverage on a held-out window. Keep the Taylor-rule and counterfactual sections, with units stated.
ideas.oracle_detail: Conjugate NIW posterior moments have closed forms: check Monte Carlo means and variances of the draws against them. Internal check: the empirical coverage of the fan chart on the held-out window.
ideas.data_detail: puremacro/datasets/data CPIAUCSL, FEDFUNDS, UNRATE (via load_macro_monthly). The corpus stays illustrative unless real statements are bundled with a licence check.
ideas.library_gaps: Check that simulate_var_paths accepts per-draw Sigma from the posterior (it takes Sigma_draws, 47.py:282).
ideas.plan_overlap: REVIEW.md:113-118; the 'policy accounting lab' brainstorm (REVIEW.md:146-149).

vets.required_changes: 1. Use minnesota_gibbs (puremacro/var/bvar.py:266), not minnesota_posterior, for draws. First fix the lambda2 dummy bug at bvar.py:241-254 (warn or raise for lambda2!=1, or use a consistent own coefficient), add a tight-prior regression test, and update the stale docstring at bvar.py:14. Until that fix lands, call it with lambda2=1.0 and say that the conjugate prior forces symmetric own and cross tightness. 2. Oracle: build the dummy block in the notebook with numpy (not the private helper). Assert that MC means and variances of B and Sigma match B_post, S_post/(nu-n-1) and E[Sigma] kron (X*'X*)^-1 within MC error, and that the Gibbs mean equals minnesota_posterior(..., lambda2=1) to about 1e-12. 3. Replace the single held-out window with rolling-origin coverage: an expanding window, origins about 1999Q4-2023Q2, h in {1,4,8,12}, central 50/70/90 bands, comparing plug-in, jitter, Gibbs and residual bootstrap. Also compare lag orders, p=1 vs p=4. State that the origins overlap (about 8 independent 12-quarter windows) and show a variant that excludes windows touching 2020-21. Reframe the question: posterior vs jitter matters little, specification matters a lot. 4. Provenance table: bundled CSVs with last observation 2026-06 and bundled in commit 8b4d1bc (2026-08-20), or record a retrieval date. Latest vintage, not real-time. Output gap and u* are constructed (47.py:135-138). The corpus is hand-written and illustrative: rename the comment at 47.py:90 and drop "official". 5. Relabel the counterfactual as a backward-looking (accelerationist) block, not a forward-looking NK model. Tie every prose number (47.py:375-378) to printed outputs, state units (pp, annualised; 12-month CPI inflation, quarterly average), and use fan_chart_quantiles central levels for both printing and plotting. 6. Write the forecast residual bootstrap by hand (no API exists), or add a small helper. Update the _es twin, docs/notebooks.md and docs/es/notebooks.md in the same change, and coordinate with the examples-4 BVAR proposal.
vets.capabilities_check: Mostly present, but the proposal names the wrong symbol and one of the functions has a bug. (1) minnesota_posterior (puremacro/var/bvar.py:40) returns only the posterior MEAN. It produces no draws, and its module docstring saying "Gibbs deferred to v2" (bvar.py:14) is stale. The draws come from minnesota_gibbs (bvar.py:266), a batched conjugate NIW sampler that returns A_draws (D,p,n,n), Sigma_draws and intercept_draws. (2) simulate_var_paths (puremacro/posterior.py:14-57) takes a per-draw Sigma_draws[d], factorised by Cholesky per draw, so the gap the proposal flagged is resolved. fan_chart_quantiles (posterior.py:60) is plain np.percentile. (3) BUG, confirmed by smoke run: _build_minnesota_dummies (bvar.py:241-254) overwrites Xd[row, col] inside the loop over equations, and the last equation's value wins. With lambda2!=1, every variable except the last gets its own-lag dummy scaled with cross_coeff. The implied prior mean on the own first lag is then lambda2, not 1. Under the default lambda2=0.5, minnesota_gibbs with a tight prior (lambda1=0.001) centres diag(A1) at [0.5, 0.5, 1.0], while minnesota_posterior gives [1, 1, 1]. On 47's data the conjugate and equation-by-equation posterior means differ by up to 0.058 at lambda2=0.5 and agree to 8e-15 at lambda2=1.0. tests/test_var_bvar_coverage.py:371 does not catch this: its DGP of 0.4 still passes against a prior mean of 0.5. (4) There is no forecast-bootstrap API. var/bootstrap.py:69 bootstrap_bands covers IRFs only, so the residual bootstrap must be hand-written: about 20 lines with fit_var, 7.8 s for 95 origins at 400 draws. (5) tone (narrative/indices/tone.py:41) runs, but on one-sentence statements it outputs only {-1,0,1}. Runtime is small: Gibbs plus 1000 paths takes under 0.3 s, and the full rolling-origin coverage run takes 1.6 s per method, so Pyodide is feasible.
vets.oracle_check: The closed form is obtainable, and I verified it. Under the conjugate NIW posterior: E[B] = B_post, E[Sigma] = S_post/(nu-n-1), and Var(vec B) = E[Sigma] kron (X*'X*)^-1. With 5000 draws on 47's data, the max absolute error of the A mean was 0.002, the Sigma mean was within 0.7% relative, and var(B) within 2.7% relative (nu_post = 168 matches). This is weak as an independent oracle for two reasons. It re-derives the sampler's own dummy block, and tests/test_var_bvar_coverage.py:183 already checks the IW mean. It becomes independent if the notebook (a) writes its own Minnesota dummy block in numpy rather than calling the private _build_minnesota_dummies, and (b) cross-checks the posterior mean against minnesota_posterior, which is a separate equation-by-equation lstsq code path agreeing to 8e-15 at lambda2=1. The coverage part is an empirical diagnostic, not an oracle. A single held-out window is too thin: a 12-quarter horizon gives only about 8 non-overlapping windows after 1999, so use rolling origins and report their dependence.
vets.data_check: The data are bundled, with no network needed. load_macro_monthly (puremacro/datasets/loaders.py:159) reads CPIAUCSL, FEDFUNDS, UNRATE, CPILFESL and NFCI CSVs from puremacro/datasets/data/. The last observation is 2026-06-01 (NFCI: 2026-07-17), and the quarterly sample runs 1985Q1-2026Q2 (166 obs). No retrieval date or vintage is recorded anywhere in the repo. The only anchor is the commit that added the files (8b4d1bc, 2026-08-20), so the provenance table must state that anchor, or the build should record a retrieval date. The data are latest-vintage, not real-time, which matters for a "real-time stance" claim. The output gap is constructed, not observed: -2*(u - rolling 10y mean u), with fillna(5.0), at 47.py:135-138, and the table must say so. The corpus at 47.py:91-104 is hand-written paraphrase, labelled "12 official policy statements" at 47.py:90. Keeping it illustrative avoids any licence question, so do not bundle official texts. The three macro series come from BLS and the Federal Reserve Board. I did not verify licence terms this session, so the provenance table should cite FRED's source notes rather than assert a licence.
vets.novelty_check: Novel within the notebooks. No notebook 00-68 (or its _es twin) and no course or curso notebook calls minnesota_gibbs or evaluates fan-chart coverage on real data. Notebook 00 v2 only mentions the Minnesota BVAR, and notebook 59 does PIT/Berkowitz on synthetic data. The same Gibbs -> simulate_var_paths -> quantiles pipeline exists only on simulated data, in puremacro/examples/bvar_fan_chart.py and posterior_predictive_fan.py. Rebuilding 47 is an explicit open item: REVIEW.md:113-118, and PLAN.md:87 ("open items (28, 32, 33, 47, 49, 59) remain open"). There is no conflict with PLAN.md:107 "SW07 policy scenarios (fan charts)", which is a DSGE model. The closer brainstorm link is the information-set lab (REVIEW.md:134) rather than the policy accounting lab (REVIEW.md:146). Coordinate with the examples-4 BVAR proposal so that 47 consumes its posterior rather than duplicating it.

ideas.title: Macroprudential GaR on real data, connectedness with a known truth, and an explicit loss mapping (rebuild 49)
ideas.question: How does financial tightness shift the left tail of GDP growth in US data, and can the Diebold-Yilmaz index recover a known connectedness structure from simulated bank returns?
ideas.description: Keep the QAR and skew-t GaR on bundled NFCI and GDP. Simulate the bank panel with neutral labels (Bank A-E) from a VAR whose population GFEVD spillover table is computed exactly, then compare the rolling estimate with the truth. Present the capital-loss mapping as an explicit assumption with a sensitivity table, and remove the 'justifies CCyB 2.5-3.5%' conclusion.
ideas.oracle_detail: The population GFEVD and total spillover of the simulated VAR are computed from its true coefficients. Optionally, ABG (2019) qualitative GaR slopes, read from the paper in-session.
ideas.data_detail: puremacro/datasets/data/NFCI.csv, FEDFUNDS.csv, UNRATE.csv, A191RL1Q225SBEA.csv; the bank panel is synthetic.
ideas.library_gaps: No helper for the population GFEVD of a known VAR; it could be computed inline.
ideas.plan_overlap: REVIEW.md:113-118 (49 interpretation).

vets.required_changes:
1. Condition on NFCI directly (ABG), not the PCA of nfci, fed_funds and unemployment_rate (line 65). Use x_t=(1, y_t, NFCI_t).
2. Make the headline h=1 via qar, which is exactly ABG's target. If h=4 is shown, build ABG's annualized average target and fit it with regress.quantreg (or add a small average-target option to qar), and label the upper tail as imprecise.
3. Pin the headline sample to 1973Q1-2015Q4 (cite SR794 p.8 and p.17). Show 1971-2026 as an extension where the upper-tail slope turns positive and the skew-t turns right-skewed.
4. Fit the skew-t to the 5/25/75/95 quantiles (SR794 p.12) with maxiter of about 2000. Report the fit residual and the success flag, limit to 2-3 fits, and assert only on GaR and slope ordering, never on the sign of alpha.
5. DY section:
   - Label the banks A-E and simulate a VAR(1) with a regime change that has a large contrast.
   - Compute the truth with var.irf.gfevd on the true (A, Sigma), and cross-check it with the A=0 equicorrelated closed form.
   - Add a Monte Carlo table of bias against window length (W=36/60/120/250).
   - Use window >= 120 and p=1 for the rolling plot.
   - Frame the question as "how much data before the index recovers the truth", not as recovery.
6. Present the loss mapping as a labelled illustrative assumption with a sensitivity grid over loss-per-pp and NIM. Delete the CCyB 2.5-3.5% sentence (line 194) and the tickers (line 115) in both EN and ES.
7. Keep the GaR section compact and cross-reference 09 and T03_C, so the DY truth/bias experiment is the distinctive content.
8. Fix the docstrings at diebold_yilmaz.py:9-12 and loaders.py:117/403, and update the three catalog rows.
vets.capabilities_check:
All three symbols exist at the paths given, and I smoke-ran each one on bundled data or a simulated VAR.
- qar is at puremacro/gar/qar.py:27. Its target is a single quarter, y[max_lag+h:] (qar.py:111). So h=4 is NOT ABG's target, which is the annualized average growth between t and t+h (ABG SR794 pdf p.9, fetched this session). At h=1 qar matches ABG exactly.
- fit_skewt_to_quantiles is at puremacro/gar/skewt.py:259. It uses Nelder-Mead with maxiter=200 (skewt.py:263) and returned success=False on every real-data input. With maxiter=2000 it converges but takes 5-19 s per fit, and alpha is poorly identified: at full sample, NFCI=+1.51, alpha is +0.02 with maxiter 200 and +3.44 with maxiter 2000.
- spillover_index is at puremacro/connectedness/diebold_yilmaz.py:25. The rolling window over 400 obs takes 0.08 s. Its module docstring (lines 9-12) still says Cholesky although the default is gfevd.
- The stated library gap is overstated: puremacro.var.irf.gfevd(A_list, Sigma, H) (irf.py:32) takes the true coefficients directly, so the population truth is a one-line call.
vets.oracle_check:
The simulation truth is obtainable. The population total is 14.10 for the calm VAR and 24.75 for the stress VAR, both from gfevd on the true (A, Sigma).

It is not fully independent, because spillover_index calls the same gfevd. Two independent checks both pass:
- Closed form: with A=0 and equicorrelated Sigma, S = 100(n-1)rho^2/(1+(n-1)rho^2). Library and closed form agree at 13.793 / 50.000 / 71.910 for rho = 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8.
- An inline companion-matrix GFEVD for a VAR(2) matches the library (max difference 0.0).

The optional ABG oracle was read this session from NY Fed Staff Report 794 (fetched PDF, text extracted with pypdf):
- "lower quantiles ... vary with financial conditions and the upper quantiles to be stable over time" (pdf p.2/p.3)
- y_{t+h} is the "annualized average growth rate of GDP between t and t+h" (p.9)
- the skew-t is matched to the "5, 25, 75, and 95 percent quantiles" (p.12)
- NFCI data start January 1973 (p.8); the sample ends 2015Q4 (p.17)

On bundled data this pattern holds only in ABG's window 1973Q1-2015Q4 at h=1: NFCI slopes are -2.34 at tau=.05, -0.86 at .50 and -0.04 at .95, and the tight skew-t has alpha=-0.83. On the full 1971Q1-2026Q1 sample it fails: slopes are -1.39 / -0.74 / +0.20, and the tight-conditions skew-t is right-skewed (alpha=+3.44 at NFCI=1.51). At h=4 with the average target on 1973-2015, the tau=.95 slope is +1.29 with a bootstrap 90% interval of [-0.32, +1.50], so "upper quantile stable" is not established at h=4. Exact ABG coefficients cannot be matched: the bundled NFCI is a newer vintage that starts in 1971.
vets.data_check:
The data are bundled and already shipped, so licensing is unchanged.
- NFCI.csv is weekly, 1971-01-08 to 2026-07-17.
- A191RL1Q225SBEA.csv runs 1947Q2 to 2026Q1. It is real GDP growth, not the deflator: its 2026Q1 value of 2.1 matches the annualized GDPC1 growth of 2.09. The loader docstring mislabels it as "GDP Deflator Inflation" (puremacro/datasets/loaders.py:117 and :403).
- The citation "FRED / BLS / Chicago Fed" is at loaders.py:409.
- The merged quarterly sample is 1971Q1-2026Q1, T=221. ABG's window is 1973Q1-2015Q4.
- The bank panel is synthetic, so no data issue there.
- FEDFUNDS and UNRATE should be dropped from the conditioning index. In the current PCA "FCI" (notebook line 65) the loadings are nfci 0.691, fed_funds 0.665 and unemployment 0.283, so about half the index is the policy rate and a real-activity variable.
vets.novelty_check:
Novelty is partial.
- Real-data GaR on US GDP plus NFCI already exists in course notebook curso/notebooks/T03_C_growth_at_risk.ipynb: QAR at h=1 and h=4, skew-t, and the 2008/2020/2022 stress episodes. Synthetic GaR with a known DGP is notebook 09_growth_at_risk.py.
- Notebook 25_frequency_connectedness.py (Barunik-Krehlik) and examples gfevd_spillover.py and diebold_yilmaz_spillover.py simulate known VARs but never compare with the population truth. No validation case in puremacro/validation/cases_var.py and no test in tests/test_connectedness_diebold_yilmaz_coverage.py checks an estimated DY index against truth.
- So the DY known-truth and small-sample-bias experiment is genuinely new, and the GaR part is a repair, not new content.
- There is no PLAN.md duplicate: PLAN.md:87 lists 49 among the open items, and REVIEW.md:113-118 motivates the rebuild.

ideas.title: Continuous-time HJB refreshed: current API, Poisson switching and closed-form checks
ideas.question: Does the implicit upwind HJB solver reproduce known limits (deterministic income, r = rho) and match an independent HACT solution once income switching is on?
ideas.description: Rebuild 22, or fold it into 56_implicit_hjb_and_continuous_kfe. Use HJBSolution attributes and the converged flag instead of dict keys and max_iter=500. State the A_z generator. Show the 3.3.0 economics (A_z=0, compute_kfe=False) next to the switching model. Check closed forms: with r = rho and no risk, c = ra + wz and zero drift. Solve the stationary KFE and continuous-time Huggett equilibrium, compared with frozen outputs from Moll's HACT codes.
ideas.oracle_detail: Deterministic-income limits with exact consumption rules. Secondary: frozen HACT MATLAB outputs, run through the MATLAB R2026a route and never generated with puremacro.
ideas.data_detail: Model calibration only. HACT fixture numbers would need to be generated and frozen (needs new data if the HACT route is used).
ideas.library_gaps: None blocking. The stored artifact is stale: it shows 500 iterations and c(0,high)=1.0, while the current library gives 9 iterations and 0.488.
ideas.plan_overlap: PLAN.md:79 ('Refresh, or fold into 56').

vets.required_changes:
1. Keep r=rho only as a remark ("the exact solution is a fixed point of the scheme"), not as a validation. The solver starts at that solution (hjb_achdou.py:653-670). Make the headline closed-form check deterministic income with r<rho (A_z=0, compute_kfe=False) against the parametric solution c=wz*e^{(rho-r)T/g}, a(T)=wz[e^{(rho-r)T/g}(1-e^{-kT})/k-(1-e^{-rT})/r], k=r+(rho-r)/g. Show first-order convergence over Na in {100, 400, 1600}.
2. Huggett GE: write an explicit brentq on sum(a*g*da)=0 with a_min<0 in the notebook, or add a small library helper. Do not call solve_aiyagari_continuous_hjb, which is capital-market only. Correct the Huggett claim in docs/vfi_hjb_continuous.md:5.
3. HACT fixture: use huggett_equilibrium_iterate.m's calibration, mapped to w_rate=1, e_grid=[.1,.2], A_z=[[-1.2,1.2],[1.2,-1.2]], a_min=-0.15, a_max=5, Na=1000, Delta=1000, tol=1e-6. Compare at HACT's bisection rate r=0.033935546875, or replicate its bisection rule (crit_S=1e-5, r0=.03, bracket [.01,.04]). The Brent root 0.03393483 differs by 7e-7. Use a tolerance of about 1e-7 (V tolerance 1e-6 plus HACT's warm start). Freeze numbers only. Do not vendor or transliterate Moll's all-rights-reserved code, and record provenance.
4. Rebuild 22 in place; do not fold it into 56. Drop the Aiyagari GE and cake-eating material, which duplicate 56, and cross-link 56 instead. State the default A_z (lambda=0.1). Show A_z=0 versus switching side by side and explain that the stale c(0,high)=1.0 is exactly the deterministic-income answer. Use compute_kfe=False whenever r>=rho.
5. Keep "HJB Solved in" and "Consumption at a=0" in the printed output, or update tests/test_challenger_m1_backward_compat.py:503-514. Rebuild the ES twin and both ipynb files. Update docs/vfi_hjb_continuous.md:105 (EN and ES) and the catalog rows.
6. Optional: add the two-state zero-flux identity s1*g1+s2*g2=0 as a KFE check, and a V0 keyword in the library.
vets.capabilities_check:
All three symbols exist in puremacro/vfi/hjb_achdou.py: solve_kfe_achdou at :422, solve_hjb_achdou at :521 (e_grid, A_z, Delta, compute_kfe and a_min<0 supported), solve_aiyagari_continuous_hjb at :849. HJBSolution (:39) has converged, g_dist, A_generator and mass_residual. Smoke runs in scratch hjb22-review/smoke1-4.py:
- Notebook 22's own call now converges in 9 iterations with c(0,·)=[0.2, 0.48829]. The stored .ipynb still prints "500 iterations" and c(0,high)=1.0000. The staleness claim is confirmed.
- A_z=np.zeros((2,2)) with compute_kfe=False reproduces the 3.3.0 economics: c(0)=[0.2, 1.0], zero drift, 6 iterations.
- The Default A_z is symmetric lambda=0.1 (:365-374).
Gaps the proposal does not state:
(1) There is no continuous-time Huggett clearing function. solve_aiyagari_continuous_hjb only clears capital against firm FOC demand (:974), although docs/vfi_hjb_continuous.md:5 says it covers Huggett. An in-notebook brentq on sum(a*g*da)=0 with a_min=-0.15 works: 9 evaluations, 0.42 s, r*=0.03393483, S(r*)=4.7e-12.
(2) solve_hjb_achdou has no initial-guess (V0) argument, so convergence from a distant guess or HACT-style warm starts cannot be shown.
(3) At r>=rho, solve_hjb_achdou gives no warning. With switching and compute_kfe=True it returns converged=True with the mass piled at a_max, and only the GE wrapper guards against this (:950).
vets.oracle_check:
The primary closed form is tautological. At r=rho with A_z=0, the solver's initial guess V0=u(ra+wz)/rho (hjb_achdou.py:653-670) is already the exact solution. It "converges" in 1 iteration with max|c-(ra+wz)|=0, max|s|=0 and max|V-Vcf|=1.4e-14 at Na=50 and at Na=200. It tests the initial guess and the zero-drift branch, not the scheme. A real closed form exists for deterministic income with r<rho and a>=0, in parametric form: c=wz*exp((rho-r)T/g) and a(T)=wz[exp((rho-r)T/g)(1-exp(-kT))/k-(1-exp(-rT))/r], with k=r+(rho-r)/g. With A_z=0 the solver converges to it at first order: max relative error in c(low) is 2.57e-2, 7.20e-3 and 1.95e-3 at Na=100, 400 and 1600 (high state 5.9e-3, 1.6e-3, 4.1e-4).
The secondary HACT oracle is obtainable and was verified in this session:
- huggett_equilibrium_iterate.m was downloaded from benjaminmoll.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ and run with MATLAB R2026a -batch in about 1 s (scratch hjb22-review/hact_out.txt). Its calibration was read from the file: s=2, rho=.05, z=[.1,.2], la=1.2, amin=-.15, amax=5, I=1000, Delta=1000, crit=1e-6. It returns r=0.033935546875 after 11 bisection steps, with S=3.968488e-6.
- puremacro at that same r matches it. c(amin)=0.094909667969/0.127755813027 against HACT's 0.094909667969/0.127755813035. c at node 500 agrees to 8e-10, g(amin)=3.948818984 against 3.948818997, V at node 500 agrees to 4.5e-9, and S differs by 3.3e-10. A replica of Moll's bisection gives r=0.03393555 in 11 steps.
Caveat: HACT is the same algorithm, so it checks the implementation, not the discretization error. The parametric closed form covers the discretization error.
vets.data_check: No data are needed; the calibration is synthetic. The HACT fixture is a handful of numbers that has to be generated once through MATLAB and frozen. Moll's code page (benjaminmoll.com/codes, fetched this session) says "Copyright 2015-2026 Benjamin Moll. All rights reserved." with no open licence. The .m file therefore must not be vendored or transliterated into the public repo. Freeze only the output numbers, with provenance (URL, file name, download date, MATLAB R2026a), from a generation script that downloads the file at run time. The whole notebook runs natively in under 1 s and is Pyodide-safe (numpy/scipy only).
vets.novelty_check:
About 70% of the proposed content is already in notebook 56 (notebooks/56_implicit_hjb_and_continuous_kfe.py):
- HJBSolution attributes and the converged flag (:68, :112-126)
- KFE mass and Gini
- the cake-eating closed form (Experiment 3, :172)
- Aiyagari GE with supply and demand curves (Experiment 4, :202)
Genuinely new and not found in notebooks 00-68, notebooks/course, curso, examples, validation, replication or tests (grep for hjb_achdou/achdou/HACT/Moll):
- an explicit A_z generator next to the A_z=0 (3.3.0) comparison
- a non-trivial deterministic closed form with a grid-convergence plot
- a continuous-time Huggett (zero net supply) equilibrium
- the first external-code oracle for the continuous-time solver
Notebook 67 does Huggett and Aiyagari in discrete time only. PLAN.md:79 lists this as "Refresh, or fold into 56". Folding into 56 would duplicate its content and delete notebook 22, which tests/test_challenger_m1_backward_compat.py:503-514 pins by path and by the printed strings "HJB Solved in" and "Consumption at a=0".

ideas.title: SW07 against the paper: optimized mode, published posterior means and data-density conventions
ideas.question: How close are puremacro's optimized SW07 mode and posterior means on the bundled data to Smets-Wouters' Table 1A, and why do log data densities differ by hundreds of log points across conventions?
ideas.description: A new replication notebook that also motivates fixing the replication cases. Run find_mode for an optimized mode and compare it with Table 1A's mode column, and a longer chain against the mean column. Verified this session from ECB WP 722: the current case targets are the posterior means, and the density targets equal puremacro's own outputs. Show Laplace vs modified-harmonic-mean densities with burn-in, and explain the paper's training-sample marginal likelihood (-905.8 in WP Table 2). Move the fixture into package data.
ideas.oracle_detail: SW07 Table 1A mode and mean columns, and Table 2, read in-session from ECB WP 722 (Feb 2007, pp.34 and 36); check the AER version before citing. Secondary: Pfeifer's Dynare replication (licence check).
ideas.data_detail: puremacro/dsge/_sw07_data.csv, a one-time FRED rebuild (tools/build_sw07_data.py), not the original vintage.
ideas.library_gaps: Replication cases score the argmax of a 200-draw chain (cases_dsge_estimation.py:84-100) against self-generated density targets. The fixture sits in tests/fixtures (:26-31), which breaks wheels. No burn-in in the harmonic-mean case.
ideas.plan_overlap: PLAN.md:99 and :189 ('SW07 against the paper', order 4, high cost; also a JOSS blocker).

vets.required_changes:
1. Fix smets_wouters.py:495-507 by adding the lagged epinfma and ewma states so cmap and cmaw enter the model, or route estimate_sw07 through load_mod(sw07_pfeifer.mod). Add a regression test: both routes give the same loglik at Pfeifer's mode on the original data (mod route -822.75). Explain the remaining 11.4-point gap at cmap=cmaw=0.
2. Fix the data. build_sw07_data.py:85 needs the 100x factor. Use the WP p.47 definitions: nominal consumption and fixed investment / GDPDEF, and NFB average hours x CE16OV / CNP16OV. Correct the 155/156 header. Alternatively use the original SW07 data after a licence check, and keep the FRED build as a vintage contrast.

The MOPM text (scratch curr-emp/mopm2021.txt, read this session) supports one extra lag. :234-240 adds y_{t-1} as a control and :685 says "one additional lag". It also says (:1059-1072) that p "should be chosen conservatively" with "no asymptotic efficiency cost" of extra lags, and (:2013-2019) that using 8 lags instead of 4 barely changes coverage.

Nuance the proposal misses: la_lp regresses on x_t with lags 1..P of every variable and no contemporaneous y. With n_lags equal to the true VAR order, x_t partialled on those lags is already an innovation, so MOPM's estimator is la_lp(n_lags=p, extra_lags=0). extra_lags=1 is a conservative choice, not "the MOPM rule".

My Monte Carlo (wf/adv-lalp-p12/mc.py; R=300, T=228, 90% nominal) agrees. Coverage at h = 0/4/8/12/20:
- Design A (iid shock, AR(1) outcome rho=0.95, n_lags=4): extra 0 = .91/.84/.81/.81/.83; extra 1 = .90/.84/.80/.83/.83; extra H (p_aug=24) = .85/.82/.76/.79/.76, with bands 1-5% wider.
- Design B (x with rho=0.99, y with 0.9, n_lags=1): extra 0 = .90/.83/.77/.73/.65; extra 1 = .88/.84/.76/.72/.65; extra H = .86/.78/.69/.67/.57.

So the H default is dominated, but one lag is not "enough" for nominal coverage. It matches MOPM Table 1's analytic LP-LA column at rho=.95: 0.878/0.838/0.806/0.814/0.833 at h = 1/6/12/36/60 (mopm2021.txt:425-436). Only MOPM's percentile-t bootstrap reaches about 0.89 (0.892/0.903/0.889/0.885/0.892), and puremacro does not ship it. The oracle has to use a bivariate data-generating process.

vets.oracle_check:
The attribution oracle is real and independent. I read it in scratch wf/curr-emp/mopm2021.txt (arXiv 2007.13888v4):
- :234-238 defines lag-augmented LP as adding y_{t-1} as a control.
- :640 says LA-LP "controls for p lags of all the time series that enter into the VAR".
- :679-686 says: regress on the full contemporaneous vector y_t plus p lags, "including one additional lag".

The MOPM Matlab code agrees (scratch wf/rev-lalp-mopm/functions_ir_estim.m:145, which calls lp() with num_lags = p-1+lag_aug). Nothing in the paper supports p+h.

Correction to the proposal: MOPM's "one additional lag" is counted against the p-1 lags needed when all of y_t is a regressor. la_lp regresses on x_t alone, recursive with x first. There, n_lags = p (the VAR order) already makes the effective regressor x's innovation, so it already matches MOPM's lag count. extra_lags=1 is therefore a conservative p+1, not "the MOPM default". The paper backs using it as a safety margin: :1063-1066 says choose p conservatively and there is no asymptotic cost, and :2018-2019 says p=8 instead of 4 widens intervals by only 3-5%.

LP-IV is outside MOPM's theorem. Their footnote 6 (:373-374) credits the IV analogue to Stock-Watson (2018, p.152), "under some conditions on the instrument".

Simulation truth is obtainable, and I ran it (scratch wf/adv-lalp/mc.py). It calls la_lp itself, with 2000 reps and a bivariate VAR(1) whose IRF has the closed form Theta_h[1, c]. Setup: x-first recursive ordering, n_lags=1, 90% bands. Coverage at h = 0, 8 and 20:

| Case | extra_lags=0 | extra_lags=1 | extra_lags=20 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stationary, T=240 | .886 / .863 / .854 | .884 / .864 / .842 | .848 / .812 / .783 |
| Stationary, T=120 | .88 / .82 / .83 | .87 / .81 / .82 | .77 / .62 / .56 |
| Unit root, T=240 | .886 / .794 / .656 | .879 / .788 / .652 | .854 / .738 / .608 |

The p+H default undercovers, because HC0 with 40+ regressors is biased downward, and it is wider at short horizons. extra_lags 0 and 1 are indistinguishable. In the unit-root case even 0 and 1 degrade by h=20.

The proposed "AR(1) with IRF rho^h" oracle cannot be passed to la_lp directly, because x and y must be different columns. Write it as y_t = rho*y_{t-1} + x_t + e_t with x iid, or use the VAR form above.

ideas.description:
_parser.py:1660-1663 replaces every parameter-only local with Const(value at load time). The regex path at dynare.py:1845-1854 does the same and silently passes on failure. As a result, every re-solve path freezes them: model.estimate via build._make_observation_eq, policy._solve_with_params/osr, smc, widgets and _gradients.

Confirmed in scratch probes. In a toy model, a local k=2a gives a variance ratio of 1.0 where it should be 4.0. In SW07, re-solving at csigma=2.5 gives sd(y)=30.1307 against 29.9343 from a fresh load; the patched copy gives 29.9343 for both.

- The initial negative log posterior goes from 1940.141 to 1932.011. Prose :331 (EN and ES) hard-codes 1940.141.
- L-BFGS goes from 1208.956 to 1237.436 and csminwel from 1631.630 to 1719.511.
- Trough-test failures go from 30 to 29. Prose :332 claims convex troughs, which is false both before and after.
- The posterior summary rows shift.

- The klein_solve warnings disappear.

Put the MCMC-diagnostic fix in the same change. mcmc.py:25 uses a short Bartlett bandwidth; mcmc.py:58-75 computes a non-split R-hat. nb42 computes r_hats and esses at :173-174 but never prints them. ideas.oracle_detail: Internal consistency first: a re-solve at theta must equal a fresh load_mod with theta written into the file. This held after the patch and failed before it (probe_sw07mod.py, sanity.py). Then compare against Dynare 8 run through MATLAB R2026a at one non-calibrated theta: steady state, decision rules and Kalman log-likelihood. For the diagnostics, use simulation truth. On AR(1) chains, Geweke rejects 35.5% at rho=.9 and 61.1% at rho=.97 against a nominal 5%. Four identical drifting chains give R-hat 1.000 non-split and 1.237 split (probe_mcmc.py).
ideas.data_detail: puremacro/dsge/_references/sw07_pfeifer.mod and puremacro/dsge/_sw07_data.csv are bundled.
ideas.library_gaps: Locals are folded at parse time. The fix keeps them symbolic, but the regex parse_mod path at dynare.py:1845 must stop writing them into params and must stop the silent 'except: pass'. Python eval also rejects locals or parameters named with Python keywords such as lambda (dynare.py:1878), which is the Galí-Monacelli failure. The ESS pair sum starts at k=1 with no monotone step (mcmc.py:107-115).
ideas.plan_overlap: PLAN 'SW07 against the paper' covers nb41, which the roadmap schedules. 'MCMC diagnostics you can check against closed forms' is a new notebook. Neither schedules nb42 or T02_E, and neither names the '#'-locals root cause.

   - load_mod: re-evaluate steady_state_model/initval at the merged params (dynare.py around 2245-2266), or treat them as a guess.
   - Add tests:
     - Toy #k=2*a gives ghu(y)=4.0 on both the re-solve and load_mod(params=).

ideas.title: Rebuild 12: can the gallery catch a wrong number? Circular references, blind designs and 13 discriminating oracles
ideas.question: Which of puremacro's 121 gallery checks could have failed on the library-sweep defects, why did none fail, and which independent oracle catches each defect?
ideas.description: Rebuild notebook 12 around the gallery's power rather than its colour. Measured in this session: HEAD f422268 passes 107/107 validation and 14/14 replication cases. A scratch copy with 13 minimal sweep fixes still passes 120/121. The one case that moves is dsge_estimation.sw07_log_posterior_at_mode (-1673.72 to -1599.73), and it moves because its target is puremacro's own output. Sections: (1) an honest recount by mechanism (see notes); (2) the circular and self-generated references; (3) blind designs: the single-cohort 2x2, lambda2=1, the diffuse limit, bandwidth 0 or cutoff 0, and a QUALITATIVE >=1 bound; (4) the 13 discriminating checks, each run against HEAD (all FAIL) and against the fixed tree (all PASS). The checks use a published table (Kiefer-Vogelsang Table I, Stata xtabond Example 4, the ShiftShareSE ADH vignette), independent software (statsmodels MarkovRegression, Dynare 8 on MMB NK_GK11_rep), a closed form (Minnesota tight-prior limit, CS eq. 3.4/3.10 weights, BQ level reversion, the SW07 ARMA(1,1) IRF, the AR(1) identification Jacobian, Dynare model-locals) or simulation truth (Geweke size, SA SE). (5) A small mutation exercise. The rebuild also removes the overclaims at 12:16-19 ('every headline estimator ... independent'), 12:172-175 ('five independent kinds') and 12:302 ('independent certification') in EN and ES.
ideas.oracle_detail: Mixed, and each oracle is named. Published: KV 2005 CAE WP 05-08 Table I p.26 (95%/97.5% Bartlett columns, e.g. b=0.5: 2.781/3.514); Stata [XT] xtabond Example 4 p.9 (WC-robust se L1.n .1934138, w .1546107; 41 instruments); ShiftShareSE vignette ivreg_ss ADH (Estimate -0.7742267, AKM 0.2403730); Stock-Yogo NBER TWP 284 Table 1 p.58; SW07 ECB WP 722 Tables 1a/1b/2. Independent software: statsmodels MarkovRegression (max llf -179.3276 on Hamilton GNP82.DAT); Dynare 8 oo_.irfs of MMB NK_GK11_rep (infl_e_ksi and i_e_ksi negative at h=0..2). Closed forms and simulation truth as listed in the notes. Every value above was read in this session from the fetched files listed in the notes.
ideas.data_detail: All inputs are public and were fetched this session into scratch: abdata.dta (Stata example data), ADH.rda (ShiftShareSE GitHub), GNP82.DAT (Hamilton's Markov1 GAUSS package), NK_GK11_rep_all.mat (Dynare 8 run of the MMB mod) and the PDFs. For Pyodide, freeze only the numbers (the reference values plus the smallest inputs), the same way validation/goldens stores its _meta. Everything else is synthetic with fixed seeds.
ideas.library_gaps: 13 minimal fixes are prototyped in scratch (sweep_minimal_fixes.diff, 137 added lines). windmeijer_correction needs a residuals_step1 argument, and ab_gmm must drop all-zero Z columns. _build_minnesota_dummies must stop the last equation overwriting the slot (force the NIW single scale and warn on lambda2). CS weights must use P(G=g). SA SE should bootstrap the aggregate. _LLSW_CV should be replaced by KV Table I. shift_share_iv needs a hat-X projection and sector_clusters. geweke_z needs an AR-spectrum at zero. la_lp's default extra_lags should be 1. bq_svar needs a cumulate mask. The SW07 spinf/sw rows need -cmap*epinfma and a same-period epinf. ms_var_fit needs a joint GLS M-step. identification() must evaluate at the supplied point. _parser must not fold locals to Const, and _ast must emit getattr for keywords. Open: GK signs (root cause not isolated), no SE for CS att_overall, build_sw07_data.py:85 (100x), predetermined_variables, and the 62-67 items.
ideas.plan_overlap: Uses the same oracles as these existing proposals, but asks a different question (gallery power, not the method): 'Arellano-Bond (1991) ... Stata xtabond manual', 'Shift-share IV done right', 'Bayesian VARs: Minnesota prior...', 'Lag-augmented LP against MOPM (2021) Table 1', 'MCMC diagnostics you can check against closed forms', 'Hamilton (1989) ... MS-AR done right', 'Gertler-Karadi (2011) against the paper and MMB', 'SW07 against the paper', 'Coverage lab: HAR fixed-b/EWC...'. It depends on PLAN's library sweep landing first, or it can show the fail-then-fix sequence itself.

The SA SE oracle is the weak one: ratio 1.144 at R=200, about 2.9 MC s.e. An exact closed form exists for the chk_sa_se design (cohorts 40/40, 20 never-treated, iid N(0,1), base period g-1, equal weights). The shared control mean enters the two cohort ATTs with opposite signs, so their covariance is -1/20. That gives Var = 0.25·2·(2/40+2/20) − 2·0.25/20 = 0.05, so sd = 0.2236; ignoring the covariance gives 0.2739. Verified here with R=3000: MC sd 0.2195, HEAD mean SE 0.2701, so HEAD overstates by a factor of 1.21.

The GK sign oracle is valid as a comparison, but the root cause is not isolated. With Y and Q matching and Pi and Rn not, a convention difference has not been ruled out.

ideas.title: Playground truth table: run every browser notebook in the Pyodide the kernel actually loads, and publish the status on the start page
ideas.question: Which of the 162 playground notebooks (70 EN + 70 ES showcase, 22 course) run in the playground's own Pyodide, how long do they take, how much heap do they use, and which oracles are unavailable there?
ideas.description: Promote this session's scratch harness to a Gate 6b. The harness is a runner.js variant that installs the wheel with micropip, preloads ipython as pyodide_kernel does, calls loadPackagesFromImports before each cell (as pyodide_kernel/kernel.py:114-116 does), runs the jupytext cells with Agg, and records time, WASM heap, file opens and missing-file probes, and 'not run' lines. Pin it to the Pyodide the kernel really loads. The built kernel bundle defaults to cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v314.0.4 (playground/dist/extensions/@jupyterlite/pyodide-kernel-extension/static/716.1d74af797dfc39b7.js), but Gate 6 pins 0.28.3 (tools/pyodide/package.json). Then render a table (PASS / PASS-with-oracle-not-run / FAIL, WASM s, heap MB) into 00_start_here, which today advertises 11, 13 and 12 as in-browser without qualification (playground/00_start_here.py:39-46). Measured: native 92/92 sources pass; Pyodide 0.28.3 passes 77/92; Pyodide 314.0.4 passes 90/92. A full sweep takes about 15 min at 4 processes on an M3 Pro.
ideas.oracle_detail: All 92 EN and course sources pass natively in this session, so any browser FAIL is an environment defect. Two Pyodide versions cross-check each other: 0.28.3 fails 15 sources (13 on import ssl, 12 on its scorecard, course 08 on parquet), while 314.0.4 fails only course 08 and 24. The same seeds are used everywhere.

ideas.library_gaps: runner.js only runs pytest-marked tests (5 functions), so it needs a cell executor; prototypes are nbrunner.js and cellharness.py in the scratch dir. The Pyodide pin must match the kernel's (314.0.4: Python 3.14, pandas 3.0.2, pyarrow 22, no fastparquet). Set packageCacheDir outside the repo: the default writes wheels into tools/pyodide/node_modules/pyodide. The dist's piplite index still lists puremacro 1.9.0 (playground/dist/pypi/all.json), so rebuild before deploy.

ideas.question: Can the third-order trust notebook show its independent Dynare evidence in the playground instead of reporting '8 of 15 checks ran and pass; 7 need the repository's Dynare fixtures'?
ideas.description: Move tests/fixtures/dynare_live (21 files, 1.2 MB: 10 npz, 5 innovation CSVs, 5 .mod files, manifest.json) and tests/fixtures/dynare_order3_pruned_moments.json (16 KB) into package data, for example puremacro/validation/goldens/dynare_live, and read them with importlib.resources where 68 now uses repo paths (lines 177/189 and 375). ideas.title: Parquet-free Forma A: make course lessons 08 and 24 run in the playground runtime and budget the heavy lessons
ideas.question: Does the ITAM browser path run end to end in the Pyodide the playground loads, including the two ENOE parquet lessons that playground/README.md tells maintainers to check after a deploy?
ideas.description: Measured over 22 course lessons. On 0.28.3, 21 pass. Lesson 08 fails at the read_parquet on line 311: no cell imports an engine, and JupyterLite loads packages only from the import text of each cell. Lesson 24 passes because lines 106-116 import fastparquet. On 314.0.4, which the kernel loads by default, fastparquet is absent and any read_parquet with pyarrow 22.0.0 dies in pandas 3.0.2's patch_pyarrow with ArrowKeyError 'No type extension with name arrow.py_extension_type found', so 08 and 24 both fail. The file schemas are plain float64 plus timestamp. Fix: ship the two ENOE tables (12,083 B and 45,410 B) as CSV and read them with pd.read_csv, and drop the engine check. Also print a budget line in the heavy lessons, measured on 0.28.3 / 314.0.4: 03 at 66/109 s WASM, 20 at 48/55 s, 23 at 36/57 s, and 25 at 41/43 s (940 MB heap; it already skips its 4000-point grids by RAM).

ideas.data_detail: notebooks/course/data/enoe_transitions_quarterly_observed.parquet (45,410 B) and enoe_stocks_monthly.parquet (12,083 B), written by parquet-cpp-arrow 23.0.1 and derived from INEGI ENOE microdata. Confirm INEGI redistribution terms.

ideas.title: Bewley classics under a browser budget: rebuild 67 with a fast mode and a heap ceiling
ideas.question: Can the Huggett/Aiyagari replication run on the playground's budget tier without silently changing what it checks?
ideas.description: 67 is the heaviest showcase: 124 s native (1,677 MB RSS), 183 s WASM on both Pyodide versions, and a 1,448 MB WASM heap. Cell 2 runs the 24-cell Table II (68 s native, 98 s WASM) plus the grid refinement at n_a=500 and n_hist=3000. Cell 3, the 25-state Rouwenhorst check, raises the heap from 441 to 1,424 MB. In Pyodide, puremacro.runtime detects device 'browser' and tier 'tablet', and runtime.fit clamps n_a=500 to 300 with a BudgetWarning (measured in 314.0.4). Rebuild: route the cost knobs through runtime.fit, keep Table II at the default grid, and report the refinement and the 25-state check as 'not run in this environment' with NaN and a status, as 68 does. Alternatively, rewrite the stationary-distribution step so it stays under a stated heap budget, for example 512 MB. 60 (163-173 s WASM) is the next candidate.
ideas.oracle_detail: Aiyagari (1994) Tables I and II as already transcribed in the notebook (AIYAGARI_TABLE_II at 67_bewley_classics_replication.py:68). The fast mode must reproduce the qualitative orderings the notebook asserts (the rate falls with sigma, rho and mu) and state which accuracy checks it skipped. Values not re-read from the paper in this session.
ideas.data_detail: Model-only calibration from the paper's parameter grid.
ideas.library_gaps: Budget aliases cover n_a but not n_hist (puremacro/runtime/budget.py _ALIASES). A sparse or iterative stationary distribution would remove the 1.4 GB spike.
ideas.plan_overlap: Touches the Done item 67 (Huggett/Aiyagari). Related to 'Discretization error in heterogeneous-agent inputs' and 'Krusell-Smith 1998 / Den Haan 2010', which will hit the same heap ceiling.

vets.required_changes:
1. Drop runtime.fit clamping and the tier-gated "not run" rows as the main route. Clamping n_a to 300 turns the grid-refinement accuracy row into a near-tautology (0.00014 pp instead of 0.0049 pp). The browser-to-tablet gate (budget.py:148) would also skip checks on desktop browsers that complete them today.
2. Implement the heap-ceiling alternative. Add a method="auto" keyword to aiyagari_rate (67:103, forwarded at 67:115) and pass method="power" only at 67:191 (refinement) and 67:239 (25-state Rouwenhorst). Keep auto for the 24 Table II cells, because power everywhere took 347 s natively instead of about 125 s. Mirror the edit in the _es twin and rebuild both .ipynb files.
3. State the ceiling as a measurement, not an assertion. Headless Pyodide 314.0.4 gave a 340 MB peak heap against the 512 MB target (1,448 MB before). Record the version, the date and how it was measured, not a claim about iPads.
4. Add a cheap equivalence check to the scorecard: one 7-state cell solved with both auto and power must agree to 1e-6 pp. This makes the method change visible instead of silent.
5. Add one markdown paragraph on why the direct solver's memory grows with n_z (T has 2*n_z nonzeros per row, then LU fill-in) and why power iteration avoids it. This carries forward to the planned Krusell-Smith and discretization notebooks.
6. Correct docs/vfi_continuous_equilibrium.md:70 and :101 (and the docs/es twin). Optionally add an opt-in, size-aware auto switch in the library, with a threshold on N_k*n_z. It should not become the default silently, because it changes the results of 52 and 56 at the 1e-7 level.
7. Retarget the follow-up list: 12_validation_gallery (1,127 MB) and course 25 (938 MB) are the heap cases; 60 is a run-time case that needs a different fix.
8. Do not claim a tablet crash. Report only the heap reduction until the Safari limit is measured.
vets.capabilities_check:
Every capability exists, but the main design, routing the cost knobs through runtime.fit, would weaken what the notebook checks without saying so. The "Alternatively" path is the one that works, and it needs no new library code.

Sources read:
- puremacro/runtime/budget.py: fit at :207-221 and override at :166-183. _ALIASES at :114-131 maps n_a to n_grid and has no n_hist alias. The tablet cap is n_grid=300 (:103-105). Every browser device gets the tablet tier (:148-151), so desktop Chrome would be clamped as well.
- continuous_stationary_distribution (puremacro/vfi/continuous_distribution.py:686-845) already has method = auto | sparse_direct | power | arnoldi. Power iteration is implemented at :803-823. solve_aiyagari_continuous is at :1302, and solve_egm is in puremacro/vfi/egm.py.

Measured natively in this session (load average about 5):
- The 25-state Rouwenhorst cell (N = 1200 x 25 = 30,000, with 2 x n_z = 50 nonzeros per row) takes 23.3 s and 1,081 MB RSS with auto (sparse_direct). With power it takes 30.2 s and 419 MB, and the rate agrees to 7e-8 pp. Arnoldi uses 940 MB.
- An LU solve of the reduced system without the dense unit-sum row (:767) still uses 952 MB, so the peak comes from SuperLU fill-in on the whole matrix, not from that row.
- The refinement cells take 17.8 s and 621 MB with auto, and 25.5 s and 288 MB with power, with identical rates (1.99681, -0.0868).
- Clamping through runtime.fit (n_a 500 to 300, n_hist unchanged) gives (1.99174, -0.08973) against the default grid's (1.99188, -0.08966). That is a change of 0.00014 pp instead of the true refinement's 0.0049 pp. The reason: a_max*x^2 with n_a=300 and a_max=300 has the same spacing near the borrowing constraint as the default grid, so the accuracy row (67:218) would pass without testing anything.
- Using power for every call keeps all checks passing at 526 MB RSS, but native time rises from about 125 s to 347 s.

Measured in headless Pyodide 314.0.4, with method="power" only at 67:191 and 67:239: all 10 cells pass, peak heap is 340 MB (1,448 MB before), cells take 193.8 s (191.1 s before), and the scorecard is identical (r25 0.6491211334, numerical error 0.0049262, shift 0.81203, packaged gap 0.002526). Scratch files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jalonso-Documents-RESEARCH-puremacro/25d917e9-42e4-445b-993d-b9f78c13ca41/scratchpad/wf/bewley-budget-rev/67_selective.py and 67_selective.p314.json.
vets.oracle_check:
The published oracle is fine but unaffected by the rebuild. AIYAGARI_TABLE_II (67:68-76), AIYAGARI_TABLE_I (67:64-66) and HUGGETT_TABLES (67:78-80) are repository transcriptions and were not re-read from the papers in this session. The notebook already asserts the orderings (67:212-221) and a transcription self-consistency check (67:143-148).

For a change to the solver method, the useful oracle is equivalence with full mode: every scorecard row must equal the current full-mode output to within about 1e-6 pp. That is obtainable. The Pyodide run of the modified notebook reproduced every row, with the 25-state rate differing from the direct solve by 6.5e-8 pp.

The proposal's "fast mode" oracle, orderings only plus NaN rows, is weaker than necessary: once the peak comes from the solver choice rather than grid size, nothing needs to be skipped.
vets.data_check: The model is fully synthetic: the paper's parameter grid only, with no data files, downloads or licensing questions. The notebook already runs offline in both Pyodide builds (sweep_lite_table.txt:89 records PASS 9/9).
vets.novelty_check:
This is maintenance on a finished notebook, not new teaching content. It rebuilds Done item 67 (PLAN.md:187, :260) and duplicates nothing.

The precedent the proposal cites is different in kind. Notebook 68's "not run" rows (68:223-227, 68:441-444) are triggered by missing repository fixtures, not by the runtime tier. No showcase notebook uses runtime.fit except the demo in 00_whats_new_in_puremacro_2_0.

The Spanish twin 67_bewley_classics_replication_es.py has identical code lines (115, 191, 239), so it needs the same edit.

The "next candidate" is misidentified. Notebook 60 has only a 219 MB heap, so its problem is run time. The next heap offenders in sweep_lite_table.txt are 12_validation_gallery (1,127 MB) and course 25_vfi_benchmark (938 MB).

ideas.title: Cross-environment validation gallery: the same 107 cases on native and WASM, with environment failures named (rebuild 12)
ideas.question: Does puremacro compute the same answers under WebAssembly as on CPython, and when a case cannot run in a given environment, does the gallery say why instead of failing an assertion?
ideas.description: The start page promises the scorecard 'right here in the browser' (playground/00_start_here.py:44-46). Measured: native 107/107 in 18 s; Pyodide 0.28.3 106/107 in 30 s with a 1,127 MB heap. The case narrative.count_keywords_known_counts gets margin inf because importing puremacro.narrative dies on the top-level import ssl at puremacro/_http.py:19. Pyodide 0.28 unvendors ssl, and Gate 2's simulated-absence tests do not block it (tests/test_pyodide_compat.py:50; tests/test_pyodide/test_narrative_importable.py:40-48 lists puremacro.fetch as browser-importable). The same import kills 11, 13, 14, 30, 33, 37-40, 47, 48, 58 and 59 on 0.28.3. With an ssl stub 8 of them pass; with the real ssl package all 14 pass; on 314.0.4 all pass. Rebuild 12 to print runtime.report(), tabulate each case's margin per environment, and label environment failures separately from numerical ones. Add ssl and sqlite3 to the blocked set, make the ssl imports lazy (also at narrative/scoring/llm.py:25 and narrative/sources/_fallback.py:21), or add 'import ssl' to the injected bootstrap cell.
ideas.oracle_detail: Case margins must agree across two numerical stacks: CPython 3.13 with threaded OpenBLAS, and WASM LAPACK under CPython 3.13/3.14. Environment dependence is real. On the same input, la_lp with its default extra_lags raises LinAlgError 'rank 119 of 124' natively but returns NaN silently at h=60 in Pyodide.
ideas.data_detail: Validation goldens already ship in puremacro/validation/goldens (package data).
ideas.library_gaps: Lazy ssl imports, or requests imports in puremacro.fetch.realtime: urllib3 reads ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION, so a stub is not enough. The validation runner should record the exception class, not only margin=inf.
ideas.plan_overlap: Complements 'MCMC diagnostics you can check against closed forms'. Also informs 'Lag-augmented LP against MOPM (2021) Table 1' through the la_lp default-lag issue in the notes.

Every capability the proposal names exists, and I reproduced the headline numbers. Scripts and dumps are in scratchpad/wf/xenv-rev12/.

Corrections to the premises:
(1) The exception class is already recorded. _model.py:136-142 stores CaseResult.error = f"{type}: {msg}". Only scorecard() (runner.py:40-55) drops it.
(2) The deployed playground does not run 0.28. The live bundle (extensions/.../static/716.f9a2968c45a70462.js) points to cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v314.0.5, where all cases pass. vets.oracle_check:
The oracle (the same case must agree across numerical stacks) is independent and cheap to obtain, but the proposed statistic is the wrong one.

Why max_margin fails: max_margin = max(|a-b| - (atol + rtol|b|)) (_model.py:69-79). The allowance dominates it, so it barely moves when environments disagree. Native vs 0.28.3 margins match to at most 4.7e-4, and most are identical.

The right cross-environment measure is the difference between the outputs themselves, taken from CaseResult.metrics[k]['pm']. Measured, native vs 0.28.3 / 314.0.4:
- 92 and 93 of 107 cases are bit-identical (relative difference < 1e-15).
- 4 cases differ by more than 1e-10; only 1 by more than 1e-6.
- The standout is inference.supt_monotonic_over_pointwise, at 4.7e-4 relative. It is a seeded Monte Carlo draw (cases_inference.py:239-247). supt.py:56-68 builds the draw factor from np.linalg.eigh, so the same seed likely gives different draws on different LAPACK builds. That is a real teaching point.
- The GARCH cases differ by about 1e-8 (optimizer path).
- Pass/fail matches in every case except the narrative ssl/sqlite3 one.

Two further problems:
- A notebook runs in one environment only. Per-environment columns therefore need frozen per-environment run_all() dumps with provenance, and nothing produces them today. No pyodide_smoke test runs scorecard() under Gate 6.
- Once imports are made lazy, no real environment failure is left to 'name'. The labelling has to be shown with a simulated-absence demo, honestly labelled as simulated.
vets.data_check:
No external data is needed. The goldens ship as package data: pyproject.toml:156 includes "puremacro.validation.goldens" = ["*.json"], and 8 golden entries are inside the 4.3.0 wheel. The case fixtures are synthetic. Nothing needs licensing.

The per-environment results would be a new artifact generated in-repo (native, Pyodide 0.28.3 and 314.0.5 dumps). It needs provenance recorded (Pyodide, numpy, scipy and OpenBLAS versions, commit, date) and must be regenerated at each release, or its columns go stale.

Notebook 12 needs a rebuild anyway, because it is stale and partly wrong:

ideas.title: What a wavelet correlation can and cannot say: MODWT variance and per-scale correlation on US output and investment
ideas.anchor_notebook: New showcase next to 26_cycles_and_bandpass; absorbs the only notebook call site of puremacro.wavelet (N08:130, :166)
ideas.question: At which periodicities does investment co-move with output, and how large must a per-scale wavelet correlation be before it means anything?
ideas.description: (1) Closed-form check of wavelet_variance on white noise. (2) Planted shared band-limited cycle, recovered by wavelet_coherence at the right scale. (3) Surrogate AR or phase-randomised null for per-scale correlation, showing that the null widens with scale. (4) The resolution trap behind N08: a series observed as 22-year averages and then interpolated carries nothing below a 44-year period. Steinhilber 2012 TSI is 22-year averages (explorations/data/steinhilber2012_tsi-noaa.txt:46,148), yet N08 reads 2-32-year bands off it. (5) Apply to GDPC1 and GPDIC1 growth from load_macro_quarterly with surrogate bands, and compare with 26's CF and BK cycles. Bilingual, with fixed seeds.
ideas.oracle_detail: For the Haar MODWT, the white-noise wavelet variance at level j is sigma^2/2^j. Over 200 draws at T=4096, wavelet_variance gave 0.501, 0.2501, 0.1252, 0.0623, 0.0311 and 0.0157, against the closed form 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125 and 0.015625. Simulation-truth null from 500 independent draws at n=181 and level 5: the 95th percentile of |r| is 0.026, 0.051, 0.109, 0.246 and 0.465 for the 2-4 through 32-64 bands. So N08's 0.4 'threshold' (N08:149) and its values of 0.21 or less are noise.
ideas.data_detail: puremacro/datasets/data/GDPC1.csv and GPDIC1.csv (FRED), loaded by load_macro_quarterly (loaders.py:111). This loader is already used by notebooks 35 and 49.
ideas.library_gaps: wavelet_coherence returns a signed per-scale correlation under the name 'coherence' and gives no significance test, CI or equivalent degrees of freedom. summary() takes argmax of the signed values (coherence.py:35), so a strong negative correlation is never reported as the maximum. Only the Haar filter is available. Boundary truncation silently shrinks the effective n. The example docstring (puremacro/examples/wavelet_business_cycle.py:4) says 8- and 20-quarter cycles, but the code at :43-45 uses 4, 16 and 64.
ideas.plan_overlap: Distinct from 'Filter-induced cycles on random walks' and 'Hamilton (2018) regression filter: Table 2', which are time-domain filters. Complements 26. Once N08 is removed, puremacro.wavelet has no notebook call site.

vets.required_changes:
1. Replace the null oracle.

ideas.title: Measurement error in a regressor: attenuation, SIMEX, and when the extrapolation fails
ideas.anchor_notebook: New lab that absorbs N12's idea. It gives puremacro.inference.simex_ols its first notebook call site; retarget tests/test_v260_showcase_replication_e2e.py:165-172 to it.
ideas.question: How much does classical measurement error attenuate an OLS slope, and does quadratic SIMEX undo it as the reliability ratio falls?
ideas.description: Monte Carlo over reliability ratios of 0.9, 0.5, 0.25 and 0.11, comparing the naive slope, simex_ols with deg=1 and deg=2, the method-of-moments correction and the exact rational extrapolant. Add a cautionary card built from N12's own numbers, reproduced here. With sigma_u=0.385 hard-coded (N12:64) against var(X)=0.167, the reliability is 0.113. The naive slope is 0.0034 (HC1 p=0.873, residual AR(1) 0.957). simex_ols gives 0.0036 and MoM gives 0.0303. N12's own hand-rolled SIMEX printed 0.0056 and was labelled 'Unbiased' (N12:170, :189). Discuss the HC1 SE under serial correlation, and the fact that sigma_u must come from data rather than a literal.
ideas.oracle_detail: plim beta_naive = lambda*beta. In the linear model, E[beta_hat(zeta)] = beta*s2x/(s2x+(1+zeta)*s2u), so the exact rational extrapolant returns beta at zeta=-1. Verified with 200 draws at reliability 0.113 and beta=1: the naive mean is 0.114 and quadratic simex_ols gives 0.200, a severe under-correction. The method of moments recovers beta whenever the estimated reliability is positive.
ideas.data_detail: Planted-truth Monte Carlo. N12's Allen and temperature inputs are a private derivation: the GPIH page lists Allen's files with no licence or terms, and the temperature column's origin is undocumented. So N12's numbers can appear only as a quoted cautionary card, not as vendored data.
ideas.library_gaps: simex_ols has only polynomial extrapolants, with no rational-linear option. It gives no standard error (neither jackknife nor asymptotic SIMEX variance). It takes a single regressor only and has no HAC option for time series. beta_mom is NaN when the estimated reliability is 0 or less (seen in the simulation).
ideas.plan_overlap: No existing title covers errors-in-variables. It is distinct from 'Instrument strength versus validity' (IV).

vets.required_changes: 1) Replace 'simex_ols gives 0.0036' with a large-B value (B >= 3000 gives 0.0061). Show the seed spread, and drop any suggestion that it differs from N12's 0.0056. 2) Restate the oracle. Add the exact asymptotic SIMEX plim (polyfit on the population curve: 0.1987 deg2, 0.1378 deg1 at rel 0.113) as the target the MC must hit. State that MoM and the rational fit are consistent but heavy-tailed at low reliability (at rel 0.113, MoM has sd 6.05 with 6% NaN, and the rational fit has sd 9.0). Report median, IQR and RMSE, and plot the distance from the rational pole to z=-1. Headline the lesson as bias versus variance, not 'quadratic fails, MoM works'. 3) Implement the rational extrapolant inline with scipy.optimize.curve_fit, with start values c0 = var(x)/sigma_u^2 and b0 = naive*c0. Or add extrapolant='rational' plus validation of lambdas and B to simex_ols, with tests in tests/test_simex.py. 4) Do not quote N12's private-data numbers as static prose. Build an N12-shaped synthetic replica computed live (n=493, var(X)=0.167, sigma_u=0.385 so rel=0.113, AR(1) near 0.96, beta near 0) and mention N12 only qualitatively. 5) Decide N12's fate explicitly. If retired, retarget tests/test_v260_showcase_replication_e2e.py:165-172 to assert that the new notebook calls puremacro.inference.simex_ols, and update notebooks/README.md:116-117. If kept, correct N12:170 'Unbiased', N12:188 '~28%' and N12:72 'bootstrap SE'. 6) Add an interval for the single-sample SIMEX estimate (pairs bootstrap around simex_ols). Keep the HC1-vs-HAC point to one sentence, since HAC barely changes it (p 0.873 to 0.896). 7) Ship as notebook 69 with an _es twin, a notebooks/README.md catalog row, docs/notebooks.md and docs/es/notebooks.md. Cross-link 38/58 and course 10_b1.

I smoke-ran it: a Monte Carlo over reliabilities 0.9/0.5/0.25/0.113 with N=400, 200 reps, B=100, a 9-point grid, deg=1 and deg=2, plus a rational fit, took 3.9 s in total. The means were: naive 0.900/0.502/0.249/0.112, deg1 0.971/0.595/0.296/0.133, deg2 0.995/0.745/0.411/0.193. Confirmed: no notebook calls simex_ols (N12 hand-rolls its own at N12:75-124). The test the proposal would retarget, tests/test_v260_showcase_replication_e2e.py:165-172, only checks that N12 imports puremacro.regress. N12 itself imports `exptools` (not in the repo; it lives at /Users/jalonso/Documents/RESEARCH/explorations/exptools) and a private parquet. vets.oracle_check: The closed-form oracle holds, with fixes. The population attenuation is plim beta_naive = rel*beta, and the MC matches to 3 decimals. The rational form E[b(z)] = beta*s2x/(s2x+(1+z)*s2u) = b/(c+z) is exact in population (derived, with b/(c-1) = beta). The proposal misses a deterministic check: polyfitting the population curve at the default grid gives the exact plim of SIMEX. At rel 0.113 that is 0.1987 for deg2 and 0.1378 for deg1, which confirms the proposal's 0.200. Two claims are overstated. (1) 'MoM recovers beta whenever estimated reliability > 0' is false in finite samples. At rel 0.113 and N=400, MoM has mean 1.96, median 0.89, sd 6.05, and is NaN in 6% of reps. (2) The fitted rational extrapolant (scipy curve_fit, a+b/(c+z)) recovers beta at rel >= 0.25 (median 1.002/0.966). At rel 0.113 it explodes: mean 0.48, median 0.78, sd 9.0. The pole c ~ 1/(1-rel) = 1.127 lies only 0.127 from z=-1. So the true lesson is bias versus variance, and it should be scored by median, IQR and RMSE, not by means. External reference, read in this session from the CRAN simex 1.8 reference manual (fetched PDF): the default is fitting.method="quadratic"; linear, quadratic and nonlinear are implemented; jackknife and asymptotic variance are implemented. So deg=2 matches the reference default.

ideas.title: Rebuild 29: SDID with the paper's placebo variance instead of a donor bootstrap that covers 61% of the time
ideas.question: Does the SDID interval that puremacro prints cover the truth at its nominal rate, and which variance estimator suits a single treated unit?
ideas.description: Start with a coverage Monte Carlo on 29's own DGP. Then add placebo (Alg. 4) and jackknife (Alg. 3) variance to synthetic_did through a vcov_method argument. Fix the silent uniform-weight fallback (synthetic_did.py:88-89) and expose n_boot_effective. Show where the placebo estimator is undefined (N_tr > N_co). Close with an honest 'Read the output' cell. N10's two simulated 'empirical' designs become labelled Monte Carlo evidence. Its Great Dying case is a warning: the planted mean post-period effect is -21.33, but tau_hat is -25.94 and the 95% CI [-29.82, -23.33] excludes the truth, with only 4 pre-periods and 4 donors.
ideas.paper: Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens and Wager (2021), Synthetic difference-in-differences, AER 111(12), 4088-4118 (reference as cited in puremacro/did/synthetic_did.py)
ideas.oracle_detail: On 29's DGP (15 donors, T=20, tau=-4.5) with R=200: mean tau_hat is -4.515, sd(tau_hat) 0.252, mean bootstrap SE 0.135, and nominal 90% coverage 61.0% (MCSE 2.1pp). On N10's Black Death DGP (5 donors, tau=-0.52) with R=200, nominal 95% coverage is 79.5% (MCSE 1.5pp). Secondary check: explorations/reviews/puremacro_sdid_2026-09-06.md section 3.1 reports that a placebo-SE transcription of synthdid covers 85-86% at nominal 90%. That is a local transcription, not R.
ideas.data_detail: 29's factor DGP and N10's sine-donor DGP, both labelled as simulated.
ideas.library_gaps: The bootstrap resamples donors only and holds the treated unit fixed (synthetic_did.py:254-271). There is no placebo or jackknife estimator. SLSQP false failures silently return uniform omega (:88-89). Replicates that raise are dropped without a count.
ideas.plan_overlap: A prerequisite for the existing 'California Prop 99 three ways... against Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) Table 1 and synthdid', which needs placebo SEs. Distinct from 'Uncertainty and coverage lab for staggered DiD' (Callaway-Sant'Anna, sup-t). Notebook 10 is unaffected.

vets.required_changes:
1. Correct the MCSEs: at R=200, about 3.4pp at 61% and 2.9pp at 79.5%. Quote reproduced ranges, e.g. 57.5-61% depending on seed and randomization scheme, and fix the seeds and the randomization scheme in the notebook.
2. Reframe the question. With a single treated unit, the placebo is the only estimator the paper defines. The jackknife is undefined at N_tr=1 (paper p.28), and synthdid's bootstrap and jackknife both return NA there. vcov_method='jackknife' must return NaN with a warning at N_tr=1. Show the jackknife only on a multi-treated variant of 29's DGP.
3. Implement Alg. 4 as an exact enumeration of all C(N_co, N_tr) assignments when that count is small, otherwise sample B assignments. Require N_co >= N_tr + 2, state the homoskedasticity assumption, and report the number of distinct placebo values.
4. Rename the current resampler to vcov_method='donor_bootstrap' and do not call it Alg. 2. Optionally add a true Alg. 2 'bootstrap' for N_tr > 1.
5. Rewrite the Great Dying lesson as bias, not variance: the Monte Carlo bias is -5.9 against sd 1.8, and placebo coverage is still only 38%. The teaching point is that no variance estimator fixes a donor trend hull that excludes the treated path.
6. Keep sdid_multi_cohort cheap by passing vcov_method='none' at sdid_multi.py:158, or by skipping variance when n_boot=0.

1. Correct the MCSEs (3.4pp at 61%, R=200; 2.9pp at 79.5%), or run R=400 and quote 60.5% (2.4pp) vs placebo 88.2% (1.6pp).
2. Say the paper's answer outright: with a single treated unit, placebo is the only defined estimator. Have vcov_method='jackknife' and 'bootstrap' return NaN or raise when N_tr=1, and when a single control carries all the omega weight. Demonstrate jackknife on an N_tr >= 2 variant: with 3 treated, placebo 91.5%, jackknife 80.0%, donor bootstrap 66.0%.
3. Fix the placebo's undefined condition to N_co <= N_tr, plus N_co - N_tr < 2 in puremacro. Use normal intervals tau_hat +/- z*SE. For N_tr=1, enumerate all placebo assignments exactly.
4. Make the fallback fix mandatory and test it on Prop 99:
   - accept a feasible SLSQP iterate whose objective is below that of w0, or port synthdid's Frank-Wolfe solver;
   - warn and count any true fallback;
   - add n_boot_effective, and optionally n_fallback.
   Pin tau_hat near -15.6 (not -27.35) and placebo SE near 8.4 against arXiv v4 Table 1 as the external oracle. Coordinate the bundled data with the Prop 99 proposal.
5. Add Alg. 2 for N_tr >= 2, or rename the current method 'donor_bootstrap' and document that it is not a paper estimator. Default to placebo when N_tr=1.
6. Present the Great Dying case as bias from extrapolating a trend outside the donors' convex hull, backed by the MC (bias -6.07, bootstrap coverage 0.5%, placebo 21.5%), not a single-draw CI. Use the reproducible CI [-29.695, -23.325].
7. Report the Black Death placebo at 89.5% for nominal 95%, and tie it to the paper's homoskedasticity caveat (p. 29).
8. Relabel or rename the simulated example synthetic_did_california_prop99.py. Fix 29's math cell and the double-robustness claim.

10. Budget runtime: about 33 s locally for R=200 with n_boot=100 plus 15 placebo fits per replication; use n_boot=50 for Pyodide. Assert coverage bands (bootstrap < 0.75, placebo > 0.80) under fixed seeds.
11. Cite algorithm and page numbers from arXiv:1812.09970v4 (July 2021), or check them against the AER version first.
vets.capabilities_check:
Every symbol the proposal names exists. synthetic_did is at puremacro/did/synthetic_did.py:134. _solve_simplex_quadratic is at :54-91, and :88-89 silently returns uniform w0 when SLSQP reports success=False. The bootstrap loop at :254-273 resamples donors only and holds the treated units fixed (:261). It catches every Exception at :265 and drops the replicate without counting it. SyntheticDiDResult (_results.py:209-252) has no vcov_method or n_boot_effective field. sdid_multi_cohort (sdid_multi.py:170, :278-306) already runs a cluster bootstrap over all units, which is close to Alg. 2. Nothing in puremacro/did has a placebo or jackknife variance; the only placebo is cdh.py's switchers test. Adding them is small: placebo is about 30 lines reusing _sdid_weights/_sdid_tau, the fixed-weight jackknife about 25; I prototyped both in scratch.

The fallback is worse than the proposal says. On synthdid's california_prop99.csv, SLSQP reports "Positive directional derivative for linesearch" for both omega and lambda. It does so even though its objectives are 134 (vs 1008 at w0) and 2939 (vs 10766). synthetic_did therefore returns uniform omega and lambda, and tau_hat = -27.349, which is the paper's DID value (-27.3, Table 1), not SDID. Using the solver's returned iterates gives -15.19; the paper reports -15.6. On 29's own DGP false failures are rare (6 of 92,800 solves, none affecting a point estimate), and the validation case cases_did._compute_sdid_3p has 0 of 42.
vets.oracle_check:
The oracle is simulation truth (the planted tau). It is independent of puremacro and cheap to produce, and I reproduced it with my own script (scratchpad/wf/sdid-placebo-adv/mc.py, run on fresh seeds).
- **29's DGP, all unit effects redrawn, R=400:** mean tau_hat -4.507, sd 0.247. Donor bootstrap: mean SE 0.131, percentile 90% coverage 60.5% (MCSE 2.4pp). Placebo (Alg. 4, all 15 placebo assignments enumerated exactly): mean SE 0.248, coverage 88.2% (MCSE 1.6pp).
- **29's DGP with fixed unit effects:** 64.5% (bootstrap) vs 87.2% (placebo).
- **N10 Black Death DGP, 95%, R=400:** donor-bootstrap percentile coverage 80.0% (MCSE 2.0pp); placebo 89.5% (MCSE 1.5pp). The placebo helps but is still below nominal.
- **3-treated variant, R=200:** donor bootstrap 66.0%, placebo 91.5%, fixed-weight jackknife 80.0%.

The proposal's coverage rates hold, but its MCSEs are wrong. For 61% at R=200 the MCSE is 3.4pp, not 2.1; for 79.5% it is 2.9pp, not 1.5.

The Great Dying numbers partly match. I get tau_hat -25.943 and a planted mean of -21.332. My CI is [-29.695, -23.325], not [-29.82, -23.33]. The stored N10 ipynb output dates from v1.0.0 (-25.247) and is stale.

What the proposal misses is that the Great Dying case is bias, not variance. Over 200 replications, mean tau_hat is -27.40 (bias -6.07). Donor-bootstrap 95% coverage is 0.5% and the placebo's is 21.5%, with only 4 controls. No variance estimator rescues it.

A better, published oracle exists. The paper's Table 1 (arXiv:1812.09970v4, p. 8, read this session) reports SDID -15.6 with placebo SE 8.4 on Prop 99. Table 4 (p. 30) reports SDID placebo coverage of 0.97 at nominal 95% for Ntr=1. I checked the algorithm numbering in the same fetched text (Alg. 2 bootstrap, Alg. 3 jackknife, Alg. 4 placebo, pp. 27-29) and against synthdid's R/vcov.R:5-7, fetched from GitHub by an earlier agent in this workflow run (wf/adv-prop99). The AER print version was not checked.

The analytic score is actually correct. Five-point finite differences through load_mod reparameterisation give -21.598608 / -451.065936 at h = 1e-4, 1e-5 and 1e-6. The cause is ScoreDiagnosticsResult.verify_numerical_gradient (_gradients.py:622-642). vets.oracle_check:
For 00_3.0 the oracle can be run, but it only checks for regressions and pins numbers that depend on the platform: the residual is 1.78e-15 natively and 4.00e-15 in Pyodide. Independent checks exist and I verified each:
- (i) Sylvester: solve the Kronecker-vectorised system (I⊗A + Cᵀ⊗B) vec X = vec D; max|X − X_kron| = 6.7e-16. Assert a tolerance rather than an exact residual.
- (ii) dghx/drho_a has a closed form. With φ = −1/(1+σ(1−ρ)), ghx = [(1+φ)ρ, φρ, ρ], which gives [−0.388889, −1.388889, 1] at σ = 1, ρ = 0.8. The library matches to 7.8e-11.
- (iii) The toy model's scores agree with finite differences to 1e-9.
For 00_2.0 §2 and §6 the proposal names no oracle, and the committed numbers cannot serve as one: they depend on an RNG stream that §1, §3 and §4 draw from first.
- §2: I ran a 300-replication Monte Carlo on the tour's own data-generating process. The planted truth (0.9 in slack, 0.4 otherwise) is recovered only at h = 0 (means 0.898 / 0.400, 90% coverage 0.86). At h = 12 the means are 0.70 / 0.30 with coverage 0.66 / 0.76. This is finite-sample LP bias from an I(1) outcome with level lags as controls: plain OLS lp_state_dep shows 0.72, and T = 800 gives 0.85. So a truth-recovery assertion across all horizons would fail.
- §6: the oracle is closed-form. At M = 0 the IM CI must equal att0 ± z·se, which gives [0.907, 1.183] on notebook 10's panel, and the identified set is att0 ± M·0.2358. The breakdown value M̄* is 2.04.
- §7 against 68's standard: canonical_growth_2nd_order(delta=1, sigma_pref=1) is Brock–Mirman, so every second-order term must be zero. The function gives max|ghxx| 4e-11 and ghs2 4e-15.

All 7 symbols exist at the stated paths: qar.py:28, fci.py:38, skewt.py:259, loaders.py:111 and :159, diebold_yilmaz.py:24, bk2018.py:9. Scratch runs are in scratchpad/wf/gar49-refute/.

ideas.question: Why maintain two notebooks that estimate the same Blanchard-Perotti SVAR, Romer-Romer LP and Mertens-Ravn instrument on the same frozen tax14 data?
ideas.description:
EVIDENCE. 14 and 50 share five symbols (estimate_var, irf, var_irf, la_lp, load_csv), tied with 00_3.0 and 43 for the highest overlap in the catalog. They use the same bundled tax14 quarterly data (14.py:132 load_csv('tax14_us_fiscal'); 50.py:70-84, 228 quarters) and the same three identifications (50.py:16-18 against 14.py:14-20).

WHAT SURVIVES. 14, which the curso T04_A mirrors, playground 00_start_here.py:33 lists and docs/ADVISORY.md:415 cites. It gains 50's lp_iv block (50.py:122-137) with the Montiel Olea-Pflueger effective F and Anderson-Rubin sets as §3b, next to the olea_pflueger_f on the proxy-SVAR residual (14.py:301). The notebook then shows one instrument through a VAR-residual first stage and an LP first stage.

WHAT IS CUT. 50's notebook-local DSA (simulate_stochastic_dsa, 50.py:142-171). By 50.py:20 it does not use the estimated multipliers, and it exercises no library function: puremacro has no DSA module, and 36.py:107 carries its own notebook-local debt simulator. Its Your-turn becomes a stretch prompt in 14, or waits for rank 59's policy-accounting lab.

SPANISH TWINS. Delete 50_es; 14_es receives the lp_iv cell verbatim.

LINKS AND TESTS. Update notebooks/README.md:71; re-point the evidence bullet at docs/notebooks.md:83-85 to 14 and drop row :186; the same at docs/es/notebooks.md:83 and :190; drop the '(`50`)' bullet at README.md:1014 and README.es.md:763. No test or playground entry names 50.

ADVISORY AND CHANGELOG. No ADVISORY entry: the instrument fix at REVIEW.md:28 was notebook-local. CHANGELOG '### Removed': 50 goes to 14 §3b.

NET. Minus 1 pair: 586 source lines, 177 code lines per language. WASM falls by 6.17 s EN and the lp_iv cell adds about 1.5 s, so the net is about −4.7 s EN. LALP showcase consumers fall from three (07, 14, 50) to two in hits.json, so rank 4's la_lp fix re-executes one fewer pair.
