The 50.py:135/139 bounds (BP impact in [-2,0]; m_rr[8] < m_bp[8]) are weaker than assertions 14 already has: 14.py:237-239, 269-271 and 352 (m_rr[8] < m_mr[8] < m_bp[8] < 0). So they add no protection. A real independent-software fixture is obtainable and I checked it in this session with statsmodels 0.15, OLS with HAC maxlags=h+1, no small-sample correction, on the same controls. First-stage robust F: 1.3471 at h=0 and 1.3621 at h=8, equal to lp_iv mop_f to 4 decimals. The manual 2SLS beta, -0.3154 (h=0) and -0.7228 (h=8), also equals lp_iv to 4 decimals. The AR statistic at beta=0 is 6.22 (h=0) and 8.70 (h=8), both above the chi2(1) 0.95 value of 3.84. That matches lp_iv's 'unbounded_rays' sets (-inf,-0.053]U[1.061,inf) and (-inf,-0.204]U[1.786,inf), which exclude zero. The MOP 10% critical value is closed-form: ncx2.ppf(0.95, 1, 10) = 23.1085. The repo docstring at puremacro/lp/iv.py:44-46 says this reproduces MOP's published table; I did not fetch MOP 2013 myself. A second hand-checkable data fact: leaving out 2003Q3 (JGTRRA, mtu = -2.858) drops the effective F from 1.38 to 0.004, and the pre-2003 F is 0.002. No paper-table oracle exists for this block. Mertens-Ravn 2013 use tax-specific average tax rates, not aggregate receipts, as 14.py:329-331 already says.
vets.data_check: Everything is bundled and offline: tax14_us_fiscal through replication._data.load_csv, and tax14_narrative_tax_shocks.csv through both loader paths, which give identical series. The sample is 228 quarters. One important data fact was missed by both 50 and the proposal: all of the MR-unanticipated first-stage relevance on aggregate receipts comes from one quarter, 2003Q3. It gives 28.9 of the 30.5 total cross-product. Dropping it gives F 0.004. Because lp_iv trims the last h observations, 2003Q3 leaves the sample at h>=14. There mop_f collapses to 0.0044, 0.0044 and 0.0043 at h=14, 15 and 16, and beta*SCALE reaches -24.0, -11.6 and -50.8. 50's executed output shows these F values. Its panels (a) and (b) plot and average m_iv to h=16, so copying 50.py:122-125 into 14 unchanged, with range(0, H+1) and H=16, would import a meaningless tail.
vets.novelty_check: The merge itself is new. PLAN.md (reviews/2026-09-23-notebook-catalog-plan) proposes no retirement or merge of 14 or 50; its only 'retirement' hit is DC-EGM. REVIEW.md:28 only repaired 50. The §3b content is new within showcase 14, but not across the corpus. notebooks/course/06_lp_narrativa_es.py:206 already runs lp_iv on tax14 (x=mtr_u, z=rr_exog) with first_stage_f and an MOP 23.1 verdict, plus a proxy_svar comparison at :235. Notebook 28 teaches AR sets on synthetic data (28.py:104-110). Curso T04_A has olea_pflueger_f and proxy_svar but no lp_iv or AR, so it needs no change. The proposal's framing, 'one instrument through a VAR-residual first stage and an LP first stage', is inaccurate. Both first stages regress the same VAR residual u_tau on mtu: F is 1.347 for lp_iv with 2 lags and 1.384 for olea_pflueger_f and proxy_svar. What is actually new is (i) a direct LP second stage against VAR iteration under a single first stage (m(8): LP-IV -5.98 against proxy-SVAR -4.32), and (ii) weak-IV-robust AR sets. These are rays that exclude zero for h<=11 (the reduced form rejects no effect; magnitude unbounded) and all-real from h=12. Notebook 35 also runs an MR proxy, which PLAN.md's rebuild of 35 would drop.

ideas.oracle_detail: 38's DGP (38.py:99-111) has a preliminary y0 = y* + u and a final value y* + d·u. **d is not a scalar.** In 38's DGP (38.py:103-111) the final value is y*+d_i·u with d_i=exp(−(48−i)/3), which runs from 1e-7 to 0.05. The population slopes are:
- β_p = (d̄−1)σu²/(σ*²+σu²) = −0.1373 over the 38 kept quarters (σ*=1.5, σu=0.6); the d=0 value is −0.1379.
- β_f ≈ 0.

**A per-series check at |z|<2 would fail.** Per-series estimates (n=38) have z-scores from −2.06 to +1.81, so two of the eight series miss that bound.

**Verdicts are not all 'noise'.** At α=0.05 the eight series give 5 'noise', 2 'indeterminate' and 1 'neither' (GBR gdp_real, β_f p=0.0074), so an 'all noise' assertion would fail.

Two assertions work:
1. **Exact in-sample identity.** news_or_noise's β equals the OLS of (d_i−1)u_i on y*_i+u_i over the kept quarters, with max abs difference 2.8e-16. This verifies the pipeline exactly.
2. **Pooled statistical check.** Over 304 observations, β=−0.155 (SE 0.018), z=−0.98 against −0.137; verdict 'noise', β_f p=0.35.

ideas.title: Are you affected? A self-check lab for the seven pending fixes, run on the reader's own result objects, with the ADVISORY entry it backs
ideas.anchor_notebook: new notebooks/69_are_you_affected.py (+_es twin), linked from docs/ADVISORY.md
ideas.question: Given a result object and panel a user already has, can a few lines of code say whether a pending fix changes the published number? The check must use only the 4.x API that is on PyPI today.
ideas.description: This draft ADVISORY entry follows the format of docs/ADVISORY.md:353 and :380. Title: '2026-09-xx — seven estimators, versions 0.92.0 to 4.3.0'. A git show over the tags confirmed the defect code is present from v1.0.0 through v4.3.0, and the SDID fallback from v1.10.0 on. The lab has one section per function. Each section runs its detection recipe on a synthetic example and then on 'your object'. (1) callaway_santanna (callaway_santanna.py:253 and legacy :339). Unaffected when res.att_gt['g'].nunique()==1. Otherwise take n_g = df.groupby(unit)[treat_time].first().value_counts() and th = res.att_gt.query('event_time>=0').groupby('g').att.mean(), then theta = (th*n_g[th.index]).sum()/n_g[th.index].sum() and compare it with res.att_overall. For the event study, it is affected wherever n_cohorts>1 and cohort sizes differ. As a cross-check, sun_abraham (sun_abraham.py:30) already weights by cohort share. (2) synthetic_did. The uniform fallback fired if np.allclose(res.omega,1/len(res.omega)) or np.allclose(res.lambda_w,1/len(res.lambda_w)) (synthetic_did.py:88-89). If there is one treated unit and res.se/lo/hi were reported, re-estimate once per donor with that donor as pseudo-treated and take se = np.std(taus). This is Algorithm 4, and colombia_reform_sdid.py:74-83 already builds exactly this loop. (3) la_lp. Affected when extra_lags was not passed and max(horizons)>1, because the default is H (la_lp.py:163-164). Re-run with extra_lags=1, a keyword present since v4.0.1. (4) bq_svar. Affected when n>=2 and a non-permanent variable enters in levels, because every variable is cumulated (bq.py:67,115). np.diff(res.irf_point[:,j,:],axis=0,prepend=0) recovers the raw response. (5) minnesota_gibbs and minnesota_optimal_lambda, which share _build_minnesota_dummies (bvar.py:242-254). Unaffected when n==1 or lambda2==1, and minnesota_posterior is unaffected. (6) gk2015_surprise. The sign is flipped against the rate convention when the inputs are futures prices; test with np.median(ff_futures_pre)>50 (surprises.py:59). The example passes 95.0 at hfi_gertler_karadi.py:36. (7) hac_fixed_b and llsw_critical_value. Unaffected at b<=0.10; affected when b>=0.2 and llsw_cv_90 was used. 'What to re-run' lists the measured cases: T05_C, Pandemics N25, informal_hours and explorations N23 (see notes). A 'How far the fix travelled' block, modelled on ADVISORY.md:397, names the Colab pin, the playground and the vendored copies.
ideas.oracle_detail: Every oracle below was verified in this session. Minnesota: the dummy-only prior mean of the own first lag equals lambda2 for every variable except the last, a closed form. The measured diagonal was [0.5,0.5,1.0] at lambda2=0.5 and [0.25,0.25,1.0] at 0.25 (scratch mn_check2.py). CS with one cohort: the fix is exactly invariant (Pandemics N11 att_overall +3.314454 before and after). SDID placebo SE: the value recomputed from J donor placebos must equal the fixed library se. Fixed-b: a simulation of the Bartlett t-statistic at T=500 with 40,000 draws gave size at the table's 90% cv of 0.096 at b=0.1, 0.123 at b=0.2, 0.149 at b=0.5 and 0.162 at b=1.0. The LLSW (2018) Table 2 values still have to be read from a fetched source before they are quoted.
ideas.data_detail: All examples are synthetic. The 'your object' cells take the user's own DataFrame or result object, and no research data is bundled.
ideas.library_gaps: None are needed for detection: every recipe uses the 4.3.0 API. After the fixes land, the lab should switch on puremacro.__version__ to show 'already fixed'.
ideas.plan_overlap: This complements the fix proposals (CS aggregation, la_lp default, cumulate=, GK sign, rebuild 29) by giving each one its ADVISORY text and a user-side check. No existing title covers a user self-check or the advisory entry.
